chapters.title: Chapter 421: The Tower—4
paragraphs: Leon’s consciousness came into contact with the treasure’s vast mana reserves. He reached out greedily, trying to absorb the mana, thinking he’d found the perfect cheat to accelerate his growth dramatically.
I desperately need to get stronger. Strong enough to use that portal guarded by the damned, angry red dragon.
That was the ideal scenario he wanted—escaping this pocket dimension through the dragon-guarded portal rather than facing the alternative Archon Vyrra had warned him about.
The monster that would eventually return to finish what it started. The creature that had nearly destroyed the Pyrrhan civilization before being driven away at tremendous cost.

She told me that facing the dragon would be like walking through a flowery garden compared to confronting that thing and its dark power, as only by surprise attack were they able to drive the monster away at that time. I definitely don’t want to be here when it arrives.
Leon needed power. Desperately. And this glowing orb seemed like the perfect shortcut.
However, the moment his absorption made actual contact with the treasure’s overwhelming mana reserves—
WHOOOOOM!
Instead of flowing into him as expected, an overwhelming force reversed the entire connection and sucked his entire mana pool completely dry in less than a single second.
"What—?!"
The shock was immediate and terrifying. His mana—all several thousands plus points of it—vanished like water down a drain.
But the relic didn’t stop there. It kept pulling relentlessly, trying to drain even the slightest remaining drops of energy from his body—reaching desperately for his Life force itself.
The suction was far too strong. Leon felt utterly helpless against it, like an insect caught in a whirlpool.
His knees buckled beneath him. His body lost all its enhanced power as his mana reserves hit absolute zero. The strength that had made him superhuman evaporated instantly.
He started dropping toward the ground like a puppet with suddenly cut strings.
No! I’m dying! This is killing me!

Gritting his teeth with desperate determination, knowing he had seconds at most before total collapse, Leon called upon his other trump card—the holy energy source that operated completely independently from his mana system.
GLOW!

Golden-white divine light erupted from deep within his heart, flooding his body with sacred power. The completely different energy source stabilized him, preventing the complete bodily collapse that would have meant death.
But the nightmare wasn’t over yet.
BOOM!

His right hand—the one still touching the enormous mana source—exploded violently without warning. Flesh, bone, and blood scattered in all directions as the limb disintegrated completely up to his forearm.
The explosive force of the treasure’s vast mana threw Leon backward with devastating power.
CRASH! TUMBLE! SLAM!
His body traveled hundreds of meters through the air like a broken ragdoll, tumbling completely out of control, bouncing and sliding across the grassland.
Finally, through sheer force of will and holy energy, he managed to stabilize himself mid-flight.
He landed hard on both feet, sliding another dozen meters before stopping completely, leaving deep furrows in the grass.
Blood dripped steadily from the corner of his lips. His right arm was gone entirely up to the forearm—just a ragged, bleeding stump remained where his hand had been.
That was... incredibly reckless and dangerous.
Leon’s enhanced mind raced through what had just happened, analyzing in horrifying detail how close he’d just come to permanent death.
If it wasn’t for my holy power stabilizing me at the last possible second, I would have died right there. Completely drained and destroyed.

Even his Phoenix Feather resurrection treasure might not have saved him from that fate. The relic would likely have just drained him to death again the instant he revived while still in contact with its surface.
He might have barely managed to teleport away with his Life in those final moments, but that entire scenario had been genuinely, catastrophically lethal.
I made a terrible mistake. I got greedy and careless. Almost paid for it with my Life.
Over the next couple of minutes, Leon stood there breathing heavily, focusing on recovery. His natural mana regeneration gradually restored enough energy to activate his healing abilities.
GLOW! SHIMMER!

His severed forearm began regrowing slowly—bone forming first from the stump, then muscle tissue wrapping around it, then blood vessels, nerves, and finally skin, until the limb was completely restored to perfect condition.
Holy energy can reattach severed limbs if they’re intact, but my arm was blown to scattered pieces. Far easier to just wait for mana recovery and regrow it entirely from scratch.
Now that Leon’s arm was fully restored and functional again, he could feel the tower’s urgent desire for its power source more clearly than before.
The mental connection he’d established when deploying the structure pulsed with need.
It’s practically screaming for connection. But how do I actually link them together?
There was no obvious place on the gigantic tower that indicated where to insert or attach the power source. He hadn’t received any telepathic instructions about this critical step either.
Let me try the most logical approach first.

Leon carefully pushed the massive circular glowing orb closer to the tower, moving it steadily toward the sealed gate entrance, and didn’t dare to try to touch the humongous mana source, now having learned his lesson.
The closer he brought the relic, the more intensely the gate began to glow with responsive blue light—a clear sign of recognition and compatibility.
Oh, it’s working! There’s definitely a connection being established between them.
When the blazing bright blue orb finally made direct physical contact with the gate’s surface, Leon felt unexpected resistance despite the entrance glowing brilliantly.
But that wasn’t necessarily a major problem.

Looking more closely now, he saw a clear marking that had just appeared—an outline of a hand on the glowing blue gate, positioned perfectly at chest height. The outline seemed to be actively drawing mana directly from the orb.
It’s too obvious. I need to put my hand there to complete the connection.
However, having just learned an incredibly painful lesson moments ago, Leon realized with crystal clarity that he needed to be far more cautious going forward.
I’ve always tried to be careful, but clearly not careful enough. This world is far too dangerous for carelessness.
His eyes burned with renewed determination and self-criticism.
I have to be more cautious. Always. Test things safely first before committing.

He didn’t want to wait years for this tower to become operational, but he already knew exactly what to do. He had his clone—he could use that for testing instead of risking his real body unnecessarily.

Even though he possessed a resurrection treasure, Leon had realized something profoundly important: sometimes resurrection might not be enough to save you. That wasn’t even far-fetched. This world was too vast and held too many dangerous mysteries. There could easily be deaths that even the Phoenix Feather couldn’t reverse, or situations where resurrection would just lead to dying again immediately.
Leon didn’t need to explain anything verbally. Both bodies shared the exact same consciousness.
A single thought was sufficient.
SHIMMER! PORTAL!
A silver dimensional rift opened directly next to him, the familiar gateway to his time dimension. His clone stepped through immediately, identical in every physical way.
The clone understood the plan instantly without any communication needed.
It walked forward confidently and placed its hand on the outlined handprint without hesitation.
HUMMM!
The entire glowing gate responded immediately, humming with deep vibration and flowing energy.
Leon’s eyes gleamed with excitement as he watched through both sets of eyes simultaneously.

Looking more closely now, he saw a clear marking that had just appeared—an outline of a hand on the glowing blue gate, positioned perfectly at chest height.
The outline seemed to be actively drawing mana directly from the orb.
It’s too obvious.
I need to put my hand there to complete the connection.
However, having just learned an incredibly painful lesson moments ago, Leon realized with crystal clarity that he needed to be far more cautious going forward.
I’ve always tried to be careful, but clearly not careful enough.
This world is far too dangerous for carelessness.
His eyes burned with renewed determination and self-criticism.
I have to be more cautious.
Always.
Test things safely first before committing.
He didn’t want to wait years for this tower to become operational, but he already knew exactly what to do.
He had his clone—he could use that for testing instead of risking his real body unnecessarily.
Even though he possessed a resurrection treasure, Leon had realized something profoundly important: sometimes resurrection might not be enough to save you.
That wasn’t even far-fetched.
This world was too vast and held too many dangerous mysteries.
There could easily be deaths that even the Phoenix Feather couldn’t reverse, or situations where resurrection would just lead to dying again immediately.
Leon didn’t need to explain anything verbally.
Both bodies shared the exact same consciousness.
A single thought was sufficient.
SHIMMER!
PORTAL!
A silver dimensional rift opened directly next to him, the familiar gateway to his time dimension.
His clone stepped through immediately, identical in every physical way.
The clone understood the plan instantly without any communication needed.
It walked forward confidently and placed its hand on the outlined handprint without hesitation.
HUMMM!
The entire glowing gate responded immediately, humming with deep vibration and flowing energy.
Leon’s eyes gleamed with excitement as he watched through both sets of eyes simultaneously.

chapters.title: Chapter 422: The Tower—5
paragraphs: Leon’s eyes gleamed with excitement as he watched through both sets of eyes simultaneously.
Please work. Please let this be simple and straightforward.

However, after a few seconds that stretched into agonizing minutes, absolutely nothing happened beyond the continuous humming. No transformation, no unlocking, no change whatsoever to either the clone’s body or the gate’s status.
Then a system message appeared in golden text before his vision:
[Ascension Tower Awakening Criteria Not Met]
[Access Denied]
Leon could feel through their shared consciousness that his clone had experienced absolutely nothing harmful—just a simple, clean rejection.
So the clone isn’t sufficient for whatever evaluation this requires. And it seems completely safe to try with my real body. This is some sort of power assessment, not an attack mechanism.

Leon immediately sent the clone back to the Pyrrhan realm. The dimensional rift could open at variable, unpredictable intervals as he’d experienced during previous monster waves, so he couldn’t afford to take any risks—even when only a couple of hours had passed since the previous festival ended.
Better safe than sorry. Keep monitoring for emergencies out there.

Now Leon stepped forward himself with determined purpose and placed his actual hand on the gate of the Ascension Tower—the structure that would become the very foundation of his dimensional realm’s future growth system.
I don’t have any causality left at all. I’ve spent almost everything on this gamble. It absolutely has to work.
The moment his palm touched the outlined handprint—
HUMMM! GLOW!
The same phenomenon occurred as before. Energy flowed through the connection; the gate vibrated with power.
Then system messages appeared in rapid succession:
[Ascension Tower Awakening Criteria Not Met]
[Access Denied]
[Insufficient Power Level]
[Access Denied]
Leon’s mind screamed internally with rage and disbelief.
FUCK! FUCK! FUCK! FUCK!
He’d invested everything—his entire accumulated fortune—and it wasn’t working at all!
Fucking hell! I was absolutely sure that if I went all out, I’d already surpassed Archon Vyrra’s power level easily. But even this strength isn’t enough for the tower to recognize me?!
Just how insanely powerful did he need to become to awaken this tower for his dimension?
As if responding directly to his desperate, furious thoughts, another message appeared—this time with a distinctly different format, which he didn’t focus much on before.
The system notification carried the tower’s logo prominently displayed behind it, indicating the Ascension Tower itself was somehow sending him messages directly through the system interface.
So this treasure is even more technologically advanced than I realized. It can communicate through the cosmic system. But that doesn’t change the fact that I’ve been completely scammed!
Leon couldn’t help the fury rising in his chest. He’d paid one hundred million causality for something he literally couldn’t even use, no matter how theoretically powerful it might be once activated!
He couldn’t help but want to scream at the unfairness of it all. The treasure’s actual worth would be far beyond his imagination once functional, but what good was that if he couldn’t access it?
Because he saw it—a progress bar showing his current power level evaluation in devastating detail:
[Current Power Level: 0.001% of Required Threshold]
[Awakening Requires: 100% Completion]
"FOR FUCK’S SAKE!"
The words exploded from him in genuine, uncontrolled fury.

So he needed to reach 100% completion of some absurd power threshold to awaken this tower? Even with his absolutely absurd cheat abilities, his SSS-class, his Divinordial race, and his incredible talent, this would take hundreds of years at minimum!
Maybe thousands of years if the scaling was exponential!
I’ve been scammed! Completely, utterly, catastrophically scammed!
Those last few hundred thousand causality he had remaining after this purchase—completely wasted now. All of it. Every plan, every preparation—rendered worthless.
Leon was absolutely fuming with rage and crushing frustration.

But one thing was crystal clear from the system messages: once the gate finally opened after meeting the criteria, the tower would absorb the orb permanently as its power source, and then it would finally awaken to full operational functionality.
It’s completely futile. Knowing the exact power level requirement doesn’t help at all when it’s impossibly, ridiculously high.
But Leon couldn’t stop himself despite knowing intellectually it was pointless.
Frustration and anger boiled over completely. He couldn’t contain it anymore.
He channeled absolutely everything he had—his holy energy obeyed his command, drawing on every reserve. His entire body brimmed with golden-white divine power, glowing like a miniature sun.
GLOW! CRACKLE! BOOM!
Then he punched the gate with absolutely everything he possessed.
BOOM!
Not once. Again and again and again, he struck the completely unyielding surface with increasing fury and resentment.
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
Each strike carried his full strength, his full techniques, his full power—and accomplished absolutely nothing against the tower’s defenses.
Far away across the dimensional realm, every single citizen suddenly felt their Lord’s overwhelming presence radiating across impossible distances—his divine power washing over them like a tsunami.
But that wasn’t the only reason they reacted so dramatically.
The sheer pressure from that distant location, even kilometers away, forced most of them involuntarily to their knees.
THUD! THUD! THUD! THUD!
People collapsed everywhere, some crying out in shock, others in reverent awe and worship.
Among them were those who’d already become Leon’s fanatical followers—people whose faith he had inadvertently cultivated simply by saving their lives during the integration.
Seraphine, instead of discouraging their growing worship, had quietly encouraged it, seeing value in their devotion.

Only Loriel remained standing initially among the civilians. Her faith lay elsewhere, directed toward the concept of Life itself rather than any individual. She wasn’t alone in her resistance—beside her stood a massive wolf and a muscularly built giant with hollowed, haunted eyes.
But even they eventually knelt not because of the pressure, leaving only Loriel—the Saintess of Life—standing upright while everyone else around her prostrated themselves.
The wolf, because of her true companion, is bound to her through a deep connection.
The giant muscular creature with hollow eyes, because seeing his daughter kneel, was her only reason for continued existence in this world.
As also the memory of the time their previous suffering flashed in his hollow eyes.
Meanwhile, Seraphine was hastily making her way toward the source of the commotion at maximum speed.
Leon!
Genuine worry filled her heart completely. Something must have gone wrong during the tower’s construction process for him to be releasing such overwhelming power.
What happened? Is he hurt? Is he in danger?
She traveled at her absolute limits, pushing her aerial flight technique far beyond what she’d normally risk.
Back at the tower, Leon continued using everything he had—not just holy energy, but every technique, every skill, every single ounce of power he could channel.
BOOM! CRACK! BOOM! CRACK!
He unleashed his most powerful attacks. Combined elemental strikes. Spatial techniques. Everything.
But the gate wouldn’t budge. Not even slightly. Not even a microscopic crack appeared. The tower stood completely unmoved despite his absolutely devastating assault.
He punched and struck relentlessly until his hands started bleeding profusely from repeated impacts against the impossibly hard surface.
Finally, he stopped—not because he accepted it was futile and pointless, but because he’d exhausted himself completely.
All the causality... all the preparation... for absolutely nothing.

He had to grind harder now, find other solutions. Hundreds or thousands of years before this tower awakened? Completely unacceptable. He’d have to find some other way to help his people grow stronger. He’d have to somehow earn more causality, even though he was completely broke.
It’s heartbreaking. But it’s reality. I have to accept it and move forward.
Leon stood there, breathing heavily, blood dripping steadily from his torn knuckles onto the grass.
Then suddenly, completely without warning, a new message appeared before his eyes—a golden transparent screen with the tower logo prominently displayed behind the entire message:
[Secondary Method Activated]
[Bloodline Evaluation in Progress...]
A loading bar began filling slowly, percentage ticking upward.
Leon’s heart started pounding violently in his chest.
What? All hope isn’t completely lost?!
But he didn’t allow himself much faith or optimism. Knowing the previous criteria’s absolute impossibility, this secondary method would probably prove equally unreachable.
Still, he stood there watching, waiting with clenched fists and racing heartbeat, unable to look away.
Please. Please let this work somehow.
The loading bar continued its agonizingly slow progression, percentage ticking upward gradually while Leon stood completely frozen in desperate anticipation.
Hey everyone, sorry for disappearing for a while without posting a Chapter. Things got a bit busy on my side, but I really appreciate you all sticking around and waiting.
Thanks for your patience and support. New Chapters will be coming soon!

chapters.title: Chapter 423: The Tower—6
paragraphs: Another message appeared on the transparent golden screen, the tower logo still prominently displayed behind the entire notification window.
[Required Bloodline Threshold Met]
[Commencing Awakening of Ascension Tower]
[Scanning for Suitable Energy Source Nearby...]
PING!
[Energy Source Detected: Worldbreath Mana Condenser]
[Beginning Integration Process]
Leon watched with wide eyes as the massive spherical orb suddenly lifted into the air completely on its own, defying gravity.
WHUMMM!
It floated toward the tower’s sealed gate with steadily increasing speed, pulled by some invisible force. The moment it made contact with the surface—
SHIMMER! ABSORB!

The orb didn’t bounce off or press against the barrier. Instead, it simply phased through the gate like water passing through a permeable membrane, disappearing completely inside the tower’s internal structure without any resistance.
Leon was watching Everything unfold with a genuine smile spreading across his face, relief flooding through him.
Finally! It’s actually working!
He felt overwhelming relief wash through his entire body. His causality hadn’t gone to waste after all—every single point had been worth it.
More than that, he was genuinely excited now. This treasure seemed way more powerful and sophisticated than he’d even imagined before purchasing it.

The tower began glowing from within, brilliant light emanating through previously invisible seams in the white stone surface. Geometric patterns lit up across the entire structure like circuitry activating.
However, the very next message made Leon groan audibly in extreme displeasure.
[CRITICAL ERROR]
[Insufficient Energy for Ascension Tower to Achieve Full Operational Status]
[Awakening Sequence Will Be Forcefully Shut Down in 10 Seconds Unless a Sufficient Energy Source Is Provided]
Leon’s enhanced mind raced desperately, trying to think of any solution.
Fuck! What can I possibly use? I have absolutely no causality left! Nothing!

Monster cores wouldn’t work—he knew that instinctively. He’d already absorbed all the valuable high-rank ones, and even if he hadn’t, they wouldn’t even begin to compare to the massive orb this glutton tower had just consumed whole.
There’s nothing. I have nothing left to give!
Then another message appeared from the system just when he’d completely resigned himself to having no choice but to give up and watch the tower shut down.
[ALERT: Alternative Suitable Power Source Detected in Proximity]
[Secret Realm Core Identified: Mythical-Ranked Treasure "Dimensional Hourglass"]
[This Artifact Meets All Criteria to Serve as Primary Power Source for Ascension Tower]
[Permission Required from Master of Dimensional Hourglass to Proceed with Integration]
[WARNING]
[Using Secret Realm Core as Power Source for Ascension Tower May Lead to Unexpected Results and Permanent Alterations]
[Proceed at Your Own Discretion and Risk]

The countdown was running out catastrophically fast! Only barely ten seconds total to make this absolutely monumental decision about using his dimensional realm’s core—the very foundation of this pocket space.
Shit! Do I risk it?! What if it destroys the entire dimension?! No, that’s just absurd! my dimensional hourglass is mythical ranked treasure!
Fuck it! Let’s do it! I have no choice!

Leon didn’t know if he’d ever get this opportunity again. What if he had to provide another massive orb just like before to keep this hungry tower active for even a single attempt? That would cost millions more casualties for another try.

And finding another suitable energy source—considering the absolutely absurd power level required just for the awakening process—would definitely take astronomical resources and time. Likely hundreds of years to locate something appropriate, or maybe he’d never even find one.
So he decided to take the opportunity right in front of him, even though the outcome was a completely unpredictable gamble.
Leon mentally confirmed the order with absolute certainty just as the final second was about to expire completely.
[CONFIRMATION RECEIVED FROM MASTER OF THE DIMENSION]
[INTEGRATION COMMENCING IMMEDIATELY]
He also sensed someone arriving rapidly toward his location through his constantly active spatial awareness.
I know exactly who that is.
WHOOSH!
Seraphine landed gracefully beside him, immediately grabbing both his hands with genuine worry written clearly across her beautiful face.
"Leon! Is Everything alright? What was all that massive commotion earlier?! The pressure—everyone felt it!"
Her voice carried both concern and urgency.
Leon patted her head gently with one hand and said with forced calmness, "Everything’s fine. Don’t worry."

But Seraphine’s sharp amethyst eyes told him immediately she wasn’t even remotely satisfied with that inadequate explanation. Her arms folded across her chest in that characteristic gesture of determination, though her body language betrayed her true feelings as she trembled slightly from enjoying the affectionate head pat despite her stern expression.

While this interaction happened between them, from deep below the tower’s foundation, thousands upon thousands of thick luminous strands of pure concentrated mana began stretching outward in every direction like roots spreading through soil.
Both Leon and Seraphine could feel it clearly—they were close enough to the tower to sense the massive energy redistribution happening throughout the dimensional space.
Seraphine’s expression became significantly more serious. Her arms were still folded, clearly waiting for a real, complete explanation.
She would have arrived much earlier if it weren’t for his uncontrolled power pressure slowing her down, Leon realized with guilt. I need to be far more careful with my strength.

Seeing her completely unyielding stance, Leon started explaining methodically from the very beginning—the purchase of the three items, the activation failure, the impossible power requirement, the bloodline evaluation, Everything that had transpired.
Seraphine listened intently to his entire explanation. She’d been worried for nothing regarding his actual safety, she realized. He hadn’t been injured or in danger.
Still, when he finished, she scolded him firmly with genuine concern in her voice.

"You need to take into consideration how close you were to the main settlement! The people of this dimension could have been seriously hurt or even killed by your uncontrolled power release! You’re so much stronger now—you can’t just unleash your full power without thinking about the consequences!"
Though privately, she admitted his anger was completely justified, given the astronomical price of those items. She’d have been absolutely fuming, too, in his position.
Leon nodded seriously, accepting the criticism. "You’re right. I’ll be much more careful from now on. I honestly didn’t think about the collateral effects in that moment of frustration."
Then she stepped forward and hugged him tightly, her voice softening considerably. "Sorry. I was too harsh without knowing Everything first."

The main reason for her panicked reaction was that she’d been genuinely terrified something catastrophic might have happened during his cultivation session or construction work—that he might have been injured or worse.
I do care about the people living in this dimensional realm. But above all else, above Everything, I care about him more than anything.

She didn’t voice that intensely personal thought aloud—it felt somewhat embarrassing and uncomfortably dark to admit. Before meeting Leon, she would never have even considered the idea of sacrificing many lives for one person’s sake. But her fundamental values and priorities had completely changed.
She also secretly feared he might not like that such a dark, possessive aspect of her personality existed if he knew.
So instead, she asked a practical question while still hugging him—this was genuinely important to address.
"What do you think will happen now, Leon? Should we evacuate everyone out of the dimension as a precaution? Just in case something goes catastrophically wrong?"
She’d been listening very carefully to his explanation about using the dimensional realm’s core as a power source.

Leon tightened his protective embrace around her. "Let’s wait and see what actually happens. I don’t think it’s genuinely dangerous—when the tower absorbed the orb, nothing catastrophic occurred. When it connects to the core, I believe the tower will just activate normally without destroying anything."
Seraphine found his reasoning sound and logical, so they both turned their full attention toward the tower.
Suddenly, without any warning, the land beneath their feet started rumbling violently.
RUMBLE! SHAKE! CRACK!

It felt exactly like a powerful earthquake at first—though nothing particularly dangerous for highly trained awakened individuals like them, especially standing on completely flat, open ground. Even normal people in the settlement would be relatively safe from this level of shaking.
Until Seraphine’s voice rang out with sudden concern.
"Leon! This isn’t just an earthquake—the actual ground itself is expanding! The land is growing!"
"Yes, I noticed that too," Leon replied calmly, his mystical eyes tracking the unprecedented changes occurring across the dimensional landscape.

While this interaction happened between them, from deep below the tower’s foundation, thousands upon thousands of thick luminous strands of pure concentrated mana began stretching outward in every direction like roots spreading through soil.
Both Leon and Seraphine could feel it clearly—they were close enough to the tower to sense the massive energy redistribution happening throughout the dimensional space.
Seraphine’s expression became significantly more serious.
Her arms were still folded, clearly waiting for a real, complete explanation.
She would have arrived much earlier if it weren’t for his uncontrolled power pressure slowing her down, Leon realized with guilt.
I need to be far more careful with my strength.

Seeing her completely unyielding stance, Leon started explaining methodically from the very beginning—the purchase of the three items, the activation failure, the impossible power requirement, the bloodline evaluation, Everything that had transpired.
Seraphine listened intently to his entire explanation.
She’d been worried for nothing regarding his actual safety, she realized.
He hadn’t been injured or in danger.
Still, when he finished, she scolded him firmly with genuine concern in her voice.
"You need to take into consideration how close you were to the main settlement!
The people of this dimension could have been seriously hurt or even killed by your uncontrolled power release!
You’re so much stronger now—you can’t just unleash your full power without thinking about the consequences!"
Though privately, she admitted his anger was completely justified, given the astronomical price of those items.
She’d have been absolutely fuming, too, in his position.
Leon nodded seriously, accepting the criticism.
"You’re right.
I’ll be much more careful from now on.
I honestly didn’t think about the collateral effects in that moment of frustration."
Then she stepped forward and hugged him tightly, her voice softening considerably.
"Sorry.
I was too harsh without knowing Everything first."

The main reason for her panicked reaction was that she’d been genuinely terrified something catastrophic might have happened during his cultivation session or construction work—that he might have been injured or worse.
I do care about the people living in this dimensional realm.
But above all else, above Everything, I care about him more than anything.
She didn’t voice that intensely personal thought aloud—it felt somewhat embarrassing and uncomfortably dark to admit.
Before meeting Leon, she would never have even considered the idea of sacrificing many lives for one person’s sake.
But her fundamental values and priorities had completely changed.
She also secretly feared he might not like that such a dark, possessive aspect of her personality existed if he knew.
So instead, she asked a practical question while still hugging him—this was genuinely important to address.
"What do you think will happen now, Leon?
Should we evacuate everyone out of the dimension as a precaution?
Just in case something goes catastrophically wrong?"
She’d been listening very carefully to his explanation about using the dimensional realm’s core as a power source.
Leon tightened his protective embrace around her.
"Let’s wait and see what actually happens.
I don’t think it’s genuinely dangerous—when the tower absorbed the orb, nothing catastrophic occurred.
When it connects to the core, I believe the tower will just activate normally without destroying anything."
Seraphine found his reasoning sound and logical, so they both turned their full attention toward the tower.
Suddenly, without any warning, the land beneath their feet started rumbling violently.
RUMBLE!
SHAKE!
CRACK!
It felt exactly like a powerful earthquake at first—though nothing particularly dangerous for highly trained awakened individuals like them, especially standing on completely flat, open ground.
Even normal people in the settlement would be relatively safe from this level of shaking.
Until Seraphine’s voice rang out with sudden concern.
"Leon!
This isn’t just an earthquake—the actual ground itself is expanding!
The land is growing!"
"Yes, I noticed that too," Leon replied calmly, his mystical eyes tracking the unprecedented changes occurring across the dimensional landscape.

chapters.title: Chapter 424: The Tower—7
paragraphs: From the translucent screen floating in front of him, Leon could see a detailed merging progress bar that had started at 10% and was steadily increasing with each passing second.
DING!
[Integration Progress: 15%... 16%... 17%...]

Leon felt mild concern that the existing settlement and carefully cultivated farmland might be destroyed or severely damaged during this violent expansion process. Still, he was genuinely happy it wasn’t something truly disastrous or life-threatening.

This expansion seemed to be some sort of beneficial realm upgrade, and he trusted completely in the people’s ability to stay safe—he’d given them more than enough cores and training to handle themselves in emergencies.
Leon also noticed something else significant as the progress bar reached 20% and continued climbing steadily.
He said aloud to Seraphine, his voice carrying concern, "Have you noticed? The mana density in the atmosphere is slowly but surely becoming noticeably thinner."

"Yes, I’ve noticed it too, Leon." Seraphine’s expression turned distinctly troubled. "This is really not good at all. The size expansion of the dimension is theoretically beneficial, but it’s absolutely nothing compared to losing the incredibly rich mana concentration that was already present here. The realm was already vastly large—we haven’t even explored its full extent yet, after all this time. This is definitely a significant net loss overall."
Leon nodded slowly in complete agreement with her accurate assessment.
"There’s absolutely nothing we can do about it now. The process is already happening. I at least hope this tower will somehow make up for the loss in the long term."

Still, he felt genuinely relieved that the time dilation inside the dimension remained exactly the same as before—that thousand-times acceleration was the single most vital aspect of this treasure for his exponential growth.
However, just as the progress bar arrived at exactly 50% completion—
ALERT!
A new message suddenly popped up in front of him with urgent flashing red text.
[CRITICAL CONFLICT DETECTED]
[Law of Time Interference Detected in Integration Zone]
[Ascension Tower’s Intrinsic Spatial-Temporal Framework Directly Conflicts with External Time Manipulation]
[Forcefully Removing Law of Time Interference to Complete Successful Integration]
[Master Permission Status: NOT REQUIRED FOR RESOLUTION]
Shit! Shit! SHIT!
Leon’s panicked thoughts raced desperately.

I don’t understand Everything being said in this technical message, but I definitely get the basic terrifying idea—the 1000x time acceleration property in this realm is somehow interfering with the awakening of the Ascension Tower!
And this motherfucking tower is forcefully removing that fundamental property from my dimensional realm without even asking!
No! Hell no! I absolutely shouldn’t have agreed to this shit! This is way, way too big a loss!
His Dimensional Hourglass was mythical-ranked, so he’d foolishly assumed nothing major would happen to its core properties, considering the tower was only legendary-rank at best.
Fuck! I was completely wrong!
Seraphine saw Leon’s face turn completely white as a ghost, genuine distress and trouble written clearly across his normally composed features.
"What happened? Why do you suddenly look so distressed?" Her voice carried real worry.
"That—" Leon’s words caught painfully in his throat. This was far too catastrophic a loss to articulate easily.
Suddenly, something absolutely fundamental changed throughout the entire dimensional realm at once.
Everyone—every single inhabitant, regardless of location—felt the profound shift in reality’s very fabric.

Leon, who possessed time affinity at such an incredibly high rank, could tell immediately and precisely that time inside was no longer flowing anywhere close to 1000 times faster than the outside world.

However, being so closely attuned to the time element at Rank 7, he could detect the new exact ratio. It wasn’t reduced all the way to match the outside world—but it was now only flowing approximately 10 times faster.
Better than a complete loss, but still an absolutely massive reduction.

To him, with his Tome of Eternal Practice—which required extremely high intelligence stats to use effectively for simulated mental training—it might not be quite as devastating a change as it would be for others like Seraphine and all the people living in the dimension who relied entirely on the time acceleration.
Seeing Seraphine’s increasingly confused and concerned expression, Leon explained in detail Everything that had just catastrophically happened.

Seraphine listened carefully and immediately realized how absolutely catastrophic the loss truly was for everyone’s cultivation speed. But she stepped forward and hugged him even tighter than before, consoling him gently.
"It’s alright. We’ll figure something out and find another method in the future somehow. Ten times faster is honestly still not bad at all compared to normal cultivation."
She didn’t carry even a single speck of blame in her voice or expression—only the firm resolve to keep moving forward despite whatever obstacles they might face.

"You just have to keep moving forward despite the setbacks you encounter," she told him with conviction. "That’s something I realized long ago when I lost my entire family. I was reminded of it again when I nearly lost my life in the Forbidden Mist. But I never stopped moving forward, no matter what."
Her eyes warmed as she looked in his.
"Isn’t that how I was able to meet you, lovely disciple?"
Hearing her genuinely supportive words, Leon felt considerably better about the situation.
He couldn’t help but lean down and kiss her forehead lovingly, thanking her wordlessly for the emotional support.
While the integration process continued steadily in the background, something else entirely was happening elsewhere in a hidden location...
Inside an unknown place deep within the Time Dimension itself.

In the middle of a dimly lit, extraordinarily ornate room, glowing gently with ambient magical illumination. Warm flickering light danced across polished white marble floors, and countless luxurious velvet cushions were scattered artfully around the elegant space.

A figure of absolutely divine beauty sat there in the center—long silver-white hair cascading down her back like a waterfall of moonlight, glowing silver-white mysterious eyes that seemed capable of piercing through the very fabric of reality itself.
Despite her overwhelmingly divine and ethereal appearance, her current actions were completely unrefined, undignified, and totally uncontrolled.
She was currently laughing so hard she’d completely abandoned all sense of decorum or composure.
"AHAHAHAHAHAHA!"
She wore an expensive, fancy, silken cloak draped loosely over her shoulders, underneath which she wore absolutely nothing for some completely inexplicable reason.
Her voice was incredibly loud—she was literally screaming with pure unrestrained joy at the absolute top of her lungs.
"THE SEAL HAS WEAKENED! AHAHAHAHAHA!"
"It’s so much weaker than before! Ahaha—no, wait! It’s not just weaker—it’s exactly one hundred times weaker than it was before!"
"AHAHAHA!"
"My future beast of a master—I think the great me is not actually fated to serve under anyone after all! AHAHAHA!"
She danced around the room in barely contained ecstatic joy, her cloak flowing dramatically.

"In a hundred years—no, no! Even less time than that! Considering I don’t have to constantly use my precious divine energy and law enforcement to maintain this cursed realm binding anymore—the seal is literally a hundred times weaker now!"
"Soon I’ll be able to break out of this ancient imprisonment myself without needing anyone’s help at all!"

She looked gleefully at a silver translucent screen floating in the air before her, watching Leon’s visibly disappointed expression as he realized he’d just lost the incredible time dilation power of his dimension.
"Ahahah! Don’t worry at all, my beastly unintentional savior! I, Xyvarithiel the Everlasting Ephemera, will definitely repay this enormous kindness properly!"
"This measly 1000x time dilation? Hmph! Just you wait and see—I’ll show you what a real, genuine time treasure can actually do!"
"But that’s definitely not enough proper compensation for saving someone as great and magnificent as me, even if it was completely unintentional on your part."
She’d been secretly watching him for an extremely long time through various observation methods. She knew exactly how incredible his natural talent truly was.
"Hmm, if it’s him specifically..."
Her divine face flushed slightly red with embarrassment.

"Yes! I’ll let him have his way with me just once as a special reward! In addition to the incredibly powerful treasure I’m going to give him in the future—that would surely be more than enough compensation for this favor!"
"Hahah! I’m so incredibly generous!"

Her face turned even redder as she spoke those words aloud, vivid memories flooding back of the hundreds of times she’d inadvertently witnessed those extremely intimate moments between him and his so-called wives through her passive observation abilities.
"Yes... just once should definitely be fine as payment..."
She muttered to herself, her divine composure completely shattered by her own embarrassing thoughts.

chapters.title: Chapter 425: Ascension Tower Awakening
paragraphs: Leon had been staring intently at the system screen for a full minute now. The violent tremors beneath his feet had completely stopped since then, leaving an eerie, almost oppressive stillness across the dimensional landscape.

His mystical eyes remained absolutely glued to the translucent golden display floating before him, watching with steadily increasing frustration as the progress bar sat stubbornly stuck at exactly 99% completion.
It couldn’t seem to move forward at all—not even by the tiniest fraction of a percent. Just frozen there, tantalizingly close yet impossibly far from completion.
Why? Why won’t it finish?

Seraphine had even asked him directly several times if the process was finally complete, her voice carrying hopeful expectation mixed with growing concern. Everything around them seemed to have come to a complete halt—the violent expansion had stopped entirely, the mana redistribution had stabilized at its new lower density, and the tremors had ceased completely.

However, Leon’s response each time had been immediate and increasingly frustrated. The system screen clearly and unambiguously showed the progress bar was still stuck at 99%, tantalizingly close to completion yet refusing to advance.
So damn close. Why won’t it just finish?

Leon suddenly remembered something potentially important from earlier in this entire ordeal. He’d questioned things before—directed specific thoughts at the normal cosmic system interface, asked the Tower directly when those unusual messages had appeared with the tower logo.
The Tower’s communication system did seem to actually provide intelligent responses sometimes, he recalled clearly. It had answered him before when he’d been confused about the power requirements.
It could just be a mere coincidence, of course—random automated responses triggered by specific conditions or keywords.
But maybe not. Maybe there was genuine intelligence or consciousness behind those formatted messages.
Worth trying again at least.
Leon decided to attempt direct communication once more.
He focused his thoughts deliberately and forcefully toward the Tower, projecting his question with as much mental clarity and force as he could muster.
What is happening? Why is the awakening of the Tower not complete even after all this sacrifice?
His mind practically screamed the inquiry at the massive structure looming before them.
However, no response came immediately to his mental question.
Only heavy silence greeted his desperate inquiry—absolute, complete, frustrating silence that stretched on for long seconds.
The progress bar remained frozen at 99% without even the slightest flicker of movement.

Leon felt his frustration building rapidly, transforming into genuine anger at the situation. He’d sacrificed everything for this cursed Tower—his entire accumulated fortune, the precious time dilation property of his realm, probably other things he hadn’t even fully discovered yet.
Answer me, damn it!
"Answer me now, damn it! Even after all this, it’s still stuck?!"

The words suddenly exploded from him verbally this time, his voice carrying raw frustration and demanding intensity. While speaking those words, Leon clenched both his hands into extremely tight fists, knuckles turning completely white from the enormous pressure he was applying.
His entire body tensed visibly with barely controlled emotion and stress.
Seraphine had been about to say something consoling—her lips had parted, genuine concern written clearly across her beautiful features as she watched him struggling with this devastating setback.
However, she stopped mid-breath abruptly, her words dying before they could form.

She’d noticed the sudden, dramatic change in Leon’s expression—his mystical eyes widening dramatically, his entire posture shifting from frustrated tension to shocked, intense attention focused on something she couldn’t see.
He’s seeing something new. A response finally came.
Leon’s mystical eyes were indeed completely focused on new text materializing on the translucent screen before him, words appearing that made his breath catch in his throat:
[Forceful Removal of Time Variable Has Caused a Critical System Error]
The text continued appearing line by line with that distinctive tower logo prominently displayed:
[Stability of the Realm Is at Significant Risk of Collapse]
[Absence of the Median of the Seal in the Newly Created World Would Cause the Awakening Process to Fail Catastrophically]
[Administrator Permission Is Required to Proceed with Stabilization of the New World]
[BEWARE: The Median of the Seal May Experience Unexpected Outcome for the Stabilization of the New World]
[Do You Still Wish to Proceed with Integration?]
[Time Given to Make a Choice: Unlimited]
Leon read through the cryptic message multiple times, his enhanced mind desperately trying to parse all the strange, unfamiliar terminology being thrown at him.
Median? What the hell is a median in this context? Seal? What seal? Newly created world?

Does that mean his time dimension had now somehow fundamentally become a complete world rather than just a pocket space or realm? What fundamental difference does that even make in practical terms? What changes between a "dimension" and a "world" when the space was so vast with mana?
And what seal is it talking about? What is this mysterious "median" it keeps mentioning?

And perhaps most confusing and suspicious of all—why was the Tower suddenly giving him unlimited time to make this supposedly critical decision, unlike all the previous instances where he’d gotten only ten seconds or less to choose?
That seems rather odd. Suspiciously generous compared to before.

However, one thing he understood clearly and simply from the message’s core meaning: for the Tower to fully awaken to operational status, and for this new world—meaning his dimensional realm—to stabilize properly and avoid catastrophic collapse, he just had to give his administrator permission.
Which seemed rather easy. Almost trivially simple.
Too easy. Far too easy.

His golden Divinordial heart was beating quite intensely and rapidly for some reason—faster than his normal enhanced physiology would produce, with a strange resonance pattern he’d come to recognize over time.
My heart doesn’t act without reason. There’s always a cause behind its reactions. It’s warning me.

One critical thing he’d learned through experience: this golden heart served as an instinctive warning system, alerting him to significant moments, hidden dangers, or pivotal decisions that would have lasting consequences.
He had to make a choice, and the obvious surface answer seemed perfectly clear.
But if it’s so obvious and easy, why does this feel fundamentally so vital?

The situation doesn’t even seem like a real obstacle or challenge, so why didn’t the system just proceed automatically like it had done before with other changes? Why didn’t it even ask for his permission when it forcefully removed the thousand-times time dilation property—something far more significant?

That was a massive, fundamental change that drastically altered my realm, yet it happened without any consultation whatsoever. So why suddenly ask for permission now for this supposedly simple stabilization?

The more Leon thought deeply about the situation, the more hopelessly entangled he became in the complex web of mysteries and questions surrounding everything that had happened during this entire process.
Too many unanswered questions. Not nearly enough information or answers.
But ultimately, he had to make a choice, and the practical reality was obvious what that choice needed to be.
I know what I have to do.
Inside an unknown location deep within the Time Dimension itself.

In the middle of a dimly lit, extraordinarily ornate room, glowing gently with soft ambient magical illumination. Warm flickering light danced gracefully across perfectly polished white marble floors, and countless luxurious velvet cushions were scattered artfully around the elegant space in deliberate arrangements.
The silver-haired woman of absolute divine beauty sat there in the center, having finally made what should have been the most joyful moment after countless millennia of torturous imprisonment.
Today should mark the beginning of her long-awaited, imminent freedom—less than a hundred years of waiting was merely a small, insignificant moment for an immortal divine being like herself.
However, suddenly, for some completely unknown and inexplicable reason, she felt intensely, overwhelmingly agitated in a way she hadn’t experienced in eons.
This feeling... what is this?

For someone who was a genuine divine being—not a mere fragile mortal—this sensation carried enormous weight and significance. She absolutely didn’t take instinctive warnings or premonitions lightly. They meant something.
It was a bad premonition, a sense of impending doom, but she couldn’t understand why she was feeling this way now, of all times.
This should be a purely joyful moment of triumph. My heart shouldn’t be feeling like this at all.
A terrifying thought suddenly appeared unbidden in her mind: Did that bastard Keeper of Dimensions somehow find out about the breaking of the seal and is now coming back to strengthen it again?
"NO! No, it absolutely can’t be possible!"

[Do You Still Wish to Proceed with Integration?]
[Time Given to Make a Choice: Unlimited]
Leon read through the cryptic message multiple times, his enhanced mind desperately trying to parse all the strange, unfamiliar terminology being thrown at him.
Median?
What the hell is a median in this context?
Seal?
What seal?
Newly created world?
Does that mean his time dimension had now somehow fundamentally become a complete world rather than just a pocket space or realm?
What fundamental difference does that even make in practical terms?
What changes between a "dimension" and a "world" when the space was so vast with mana?
And what seal is it talking about?
What is this mysterious "median" it keeps mentioning?

And perhaps most confusing and suspicious of all—why was the Tower suddenly giving him unlimited time to make this supposedly critical decision, unlike all the previous instances where he’d gotten only ten seconds or less to choose?
That seems rather odd.
Suspiciously generous compared to before.

However, one thing he understood clearly and simply from the message’s core meaning: for the Tower to fully awaken to operational status, and for this new world—meaning his dimensional realm—to stabilize properly and avoid catastrophic collapse, he just had to give his administrator permission.
Which seemed rather easy.
Almost trivially simple.
Too easy.
Far too easy.

His golden Divinordial heart was beating quite intensely and rapidly for some reason—faster than his normal enhanced physiology would produce, with a strange resonance pattern he’d come to recognize over time.
My heart doesn’t act without reason.
There’s always a cause behind its reactions.
It’s warning me.

One critical thing he’d learned through experience: this golden heart served as an instinctive warning system, alerting him to significant moments, hidden dangers, or pivotal decisions that would have lasting consequences.
He had to make a choice, and the obvious surface answer seemed perfectly clear.
But if it’s so obvious and easy, why does this feel fundamentally so vital?
The situation doesn’t even seem like a real obstacle or challenge, so why didn’t the system just proceed automatically like it had done before with other changes?
Why didn’t it even ask for his permission when it forcefully removed the thousand-times time dilation property—something far more significant?
That was a massive, fundamental change that drastically altered my realm, yet it happened without any consultation whatsoever.
So why suddenly ask for permission now for this supposedly simple stabilization?

The more Leon thought deeply about the situation, the more hopelessly entangled he became in the complex web of mysteries and questions surrounding everything that had happened during this entire process.
Too many unanswered questions.
Not nearly enough information or answers.
But ultimately, he had to make a choice, and the practical reality was obvious what that choice needed to be.
I know what I have to do.
Inside an unknown location deep within the Time Dimension itself.
In the middle of a dimly lit, extraordinarily ornate room, glowing gently with soft ambient magical illumination.

Warm flickering light danced gracefully across perfectly polished white marble floors, and countless luxurious velvet cushions were scattered artfully around the elegant space in deliberate arrangements.
The silver-haired woman of absolute divine beauty sat there in the center, having finally made what should have been the most joyful moment after countless millennia of torturous imprisonment.
Today should mark the beginning of her long-awaited, imminent freedom—less than a hundred years of waiting was merely a small, insignificant moment for an immortal divine being like herself.
However, suddenly, for some completely unknown and inexplicable reason, she felt intensely, overwhelmingly agitated in a way she hadn’t experienced in eons.
This feeling... what is this?
For someone who was a genuine divine being—not a mere fragile mortal—this sensation carried enormous weight and significance.
She absolutely didn’t take instinctive warnings or premonitions lightly.
They meant something.
It was a bad premonition, a sense of impending doom, but she couldn’t understand why she was feeling this way now, of all times.
This should be a purely joyful moment of triumph.
My heart shouldn’t be feeling like this at all.
A terrifying thought suddenly appeared unbidden in her mind: Did that bastard Keeper of Dimensions somehow find out about the breaking of the seal and is now coming back to strengthen it again?
"NO!
No, it absolutely can’t be possible!"

chapters.title: Chapter 426: Ascension Tower Awakening—2
paragraphs: "NO! No, it absolutely can’t be possible!"
She spoke aloud to the empty room, her divine voice trembling slightly with unusual emotion.

For millions upon millions of years, I was not sitting idle in this cursed prison. This is not possible. While I still can’t break the seal myself through direct force, it’s been so incredibly long since I successfully severed all mystical connections with that bastard. He won’t be able to find me or track me even if the seal weakens significantly or breaks entirely.

But she felt even more intensely agitated and distressed knowing it was something completely unknown, causing this overwhelming sense of dread. There were not many beings in this entire universe who could make her feel genuinely threatened, even in her significantly weakened state after millions of years of imprisonment. She could escape from most conceivable dangers without serious worry.
So why is my heart filled with such profound dread right now?

There was no other choice available. The complex divination spell she’d been carefully trying to observe Leon’s future—which was already the absolute highest grade available in existence—she canceled immediately with a gesture.

It would take far too much time and divine energy to maintain properly. She’d been trying unsuccessfully for years to divine his future trajectory, which should have been trivially simple given how weak he currently was. That extraordinary difficulty had already made her realize he was someone extraordinarily special—protected by fate itself.
But now I need to divine my own immediate future. See what danger awaits me specifically.

However, when she attempted to cast the grand divination spell on herself to see her own fate, she couldn’t see anything at all. Complete blindness. The exact same phenomenon as when she’d tried repeatedly to divine Leon’s future—absolute inability to perceive anything.
This is fundamentally wrong. Very, very wrong.
Her brilliant mind reached an inevitable, terrifying conclusion: whatever was currently happening was directly and intimately connected to that same boy, Leon. The anomaly she’d been watching.
The divination arts—where she was acknowledged as second in absolute mastery to only one other being in the entire universe—completely not working at all was absolutely abnormal and unprecedented.
She suddenly sensed something approaching—something massive and inevitable.
BURST!

Her divine aura exploded forth violently with the full remaining amount of divine energy she had carefully conserved. The Wheel of Time manifested dramatically around her—a construct of pure, concentrated temporal law made visible.
STOP!
She had completely frozen time within her domain, stopping everything in perfect stasis within her sphere of influence.

She was fully prepared and ready to completely obliterate the existence of whatever mysterious force was making her feel this existential dread. She felt it was impossibly close now—right here in her sanctuary.
However, her ancient eyes suddenly locked onto something that made her divine blood run cold.
The massive golden circular chamber around which multiple concentric rings were constantly rotating in complex patterns—the prison that had successfully held her captive for countless eons.

The ancient divine language inscribed on every surface of the rings was actively changing right before her disbelieving eyes. Sacred symbols shifting position, rearranging themselves, transforming into entirely new configurations, she didn’t recognize.
Seeing that impossible sight, her eyes dilated massively with pure, primal terror. Her entire divine body shuddered involuntarily with genuine fear.
"NOOOO! WHAT IS HAPPENING?! WHO IS DOING THIS?!"
Her voice echoed through the frozen time with desperate panic.

She couldn’t tell what was actually occurring or who was behind it, but the more the ancient symbols changed and rearranged, the heavier and more oppressive her heart felt. She couldn’t even identify which source or unknown power was causing this fundamental transformation of her prison.
This shouldn’t be remotely possible! The seal was created by the Keeper!
She tried desperately to stop the changes, throwing her considerable remaining divine power directly against the alterations with everything she had.

But she couldn’t halt it even slightly. More importantly—horrifyingly—all her divine energy was being actively and forcefully sucked out of her against her will and used to fuel the changes to the prison in some twisted, incomprehensible way she couldn’t understand.
My own power is being turned against me! Used to strengthen my own prison!
BURST! CRACK! SNAP!

Massive chains suddenly exploded outward violently from all around the circular prison structure, emerging from impossible angles. Her carefully maintained time-stop domain shattered instantly like glass—she had absolutely no energy left to maintain it anymore.

Even as a weakened divine being, she was still ridiculously powerful with just her physical body alone. She could still manipulate time to some significant extent using the natural ambient mana flowing around her without needing to expend precious divine energy.
However, the massive chains latched around her limbs with impossible speed before she could properly react or defend herself.
The moment they made physical contact with her divine form, her soul shuddered violently and painfully.
"NOOOOOOO!"
The scream tore from her throat involuntarily.

In the next horrifying instant, she saw her own divine body dropping completely lifelessly to the cold marble floor as her soul was forcefully separated from her physical form by an irresistible force.
She felt utterly helpless—a sensation she genuinely hadn’t experienced in millions of years of existence.
She tried desperately to escape, to resist with every technique she knew, to fight back with everything she had remaining.
I can’t! The chains won’t release! They’re dragging me!

She felt herself being pulled somewhere unknown—dragged forcefully through space and dimensions against her will by chains she couldn’t break. Her consciousness began blurring rapidly, fading dangerously at the edges like dissipating smoke.
Her last coherent thought before complete darkness claimed her awareness: I don’t want to die. Not like this. Not after enduring and suffering for so impossibly long.
Divine tears formed in her fading eyes as her awareness finally scattered into nothing.

Leon stood firmly in front of the massive Tower, looking intently at the system screen, and watched with held breath as the progress bar suddenly jumped from 99% directly to 100% right before his eyes in a single instant.
DING!

He’d been mentally prepared and ready for something absolutely catastrophic to happen—the system had made it seem monumentally important and potentially dangerous by asking his permission in that unusual, formal way with unlimited time.
However, the actual result was rather anticlimactic and underwhelming.
The system simply displayed a straightforward, simple message without any fanfare:
[Awakening of the Ascension Tower Completed Successfully]

The previously sealed gate that Leon had tried unsuccessfully to enter before had transformed into a gently swirling portal of blue-white energy. Other than that single change, nothing particularly dramatic or destructive occurred around them.

The ground beneath their feet and the mana distribution throughout the space felt noticeably more stable than before. Everything around him felt subtly different despite appearing largely the same visually—a fundamental change in atmosphere and essence rather than visible physical structure.
That’s it? After all that ominous buildup and warnings?
Suddenly, without any warning, a massive barrage of system messages appeared in rapid succession, flooding his entire vision with notifications:
[You Have Earned the Title: World Keeper (Legendary)]
[A New Item with Potential Beyond Divine Rank Has Been Born Through Your Direct Influence]
[You Have Earned the Title: Creator (Mythic)]
[You Have Become One of the Few Ascension Tower Owners in the Solmyra Universe]
[You Have Earned the Title: Path Forger (Epic)]
[You have become a low-level administrator of the Tower and the Owner of Ascension Tower No. X3301]
Shit! Look at all these rewards!

Seeing the sheer overwhelming amount of notifications from the system appearing one after another, Leon immediately realized with growing excitement that this Tower was definitely not a bad deal at all, despite all the significant hiccups, painful sacrifices, and setbacks that had come during the entire activation process.
A genuine smile of satisfaction spread across his face as he eagerly started reading through the detailed information about each new title he’d just earned, examining their effects and benefits.

Seraphine, who was standing supportively next to him throughout everything, saw him smile with genuine satisfaction and relief. She immediately understood intuitively that something very good must have finally happened to him after all the stress.
That’s the expression of someone who just gained something tremendously valuable.
She felt genuinely happy seeing him like that—finally relieved and content after enduring so much stress and devastating setbacks during this entire ordeal.

chapters.title: Chapter 427: Entering the Tower
paragraphs: Leon looked at the impressive list of titles he’d just earned, feeling genuinely satisfied with the substantial rewards despite all the painful setbacks and enormous sacrifices.
World Keeper, Creator, Path Forger... these sound incredibly valuable.

However, he didn’t bother checking their detailed effects or specific benefits for now. There would be plenty of time later to examine those thoroughly and understand exactly what advantages each title provided.
Right now, what he was most curious about—what truly captured his attention—was the tower itself. The actual physical structure he’d sacrificed absolutely everything to awaken.
His mystical eyes focused intently on the shining blue-white portal that had replaced the previously sealed gate. The swirling energy called to him with an almost magnetic, irresistible pull.
I want to enter. Need to see what’s actually inside this thing.
Leon turned to Seraphine, who was still standing supportively beside him throughout this entire ordeal.
"Do you want to accompany me inside? Explore the tower together?"

Due to the privilege of being designated the low-level tower administrator—a title that had just been officially granted to him through the system—basic foundational information about the tower had automatically flooded into his mind the precise moment the awakening process completed successfully.
Let me process what I actually know now...

The tower held many treasures and riches beyond measure, the information told him clearly and unambiguously. Resources that could accelerate cultivation speeds dramatically, artifacts of immense power that could change destinies, knowledge that had been lost to time itself across millennia.

But all of it—every single benefit—came with corresponding risk and genuine danger. The challenges inside were specifically designed to push people to their absolute limits and force them to break through or die trying.
There were a total of one thousand floors in the complete tower structure, according to the administrator’s knowledge he’d received.
One thousand floors? Looking at the physical size of the tower, even as massive as it is, that number seems absurdly high.

But then again, it wasn’t particularly strange or impossible when he considered it properly with his enhanced intelligence. His Dimensional Hourglass could contain an entire vast realm with countless kilometers of space inside a relatively small artifact you could hold in your hand. Spatial compression and dimensional folding were clearly common fundamental techniques at this level of advanced cosmic engineering.

The information also revealed something fascinating about the privilege and authority system: as higher floors of the tower were successfully cleared under his administration and oversight, the greater his privileges and authority would progressively become, and the more comprehensive knowledge he would systematically gain about the tower’s true nature and ultimate cosmic purpose.
So I have to earn a deeper understanding through actual achievement and progress. Nothing is given freely.
And there was something else—something particularly significant that made Leon’s heart race with both genuine excitement and real trepidation.

The basic information had told him explicitly that there were thousands upon thousands of these Ascension Towers scattered strategically across the Solmyra Universe, which was his universe name, and countless others which he didn’t know of, and they were all somehow fundamentally connected to each other somewhere in a grand network, serving some unified purpose that transcended individual worlds and civilizations.
But what purpose exactly? What’s the ultimate goal of this system?
That was apparently the strict limit of what he could learn at his current low administrator level.

To discover more—to truly understand the towers’ actual function in the universe’s grand design—he would have to physically climb the tower himself and reach significantly higher floors to unlock deeper knowledge.
But one absolutely critical piece of information stood out above all others in sheer importance:

The 50th floor was specifically and explicitly described as the "true beginning" of the tower system—a gateway floor where countless different worlds, which contained their own individual Ascension Towers, would suddenly connect together, allowing people from completely different civilizations and realms to traverse between worlds and interact directly with each other inside the tower and even outside.
That floor opens everything up completely. Incredible opportunity for growth, resources, knowledge...

But also tremendous risk of invasion, conflict, and destruction. Once that critical floor was cleared, powerful hostile forces from other advanced worlds could potentially infiltrate his dimensional realm through the tower connection without facing significant barriers to entry.
However, there was a grace period built carefully into the system—a protective buffer mechanism to prevent immediate catastrophe.
Ten years. That’s the critical time limit I have to remember.

If he failed to clear another floor within ten years after reaching any major milestone, anyone from connected worlds could infiltrate his realm without any restrictions whatsoever. But before reaching that dangerous threshold point, without his explicit permission as the tower’s administrator, absolutely no one could enter his world through his specific tower gateway.

Leon felt a genuine spike of fear considering that nightmare scenario playing out—hostile forces from technologically or magically advanced civilizations pouring endlessly into his realm, threatening and killing everyone he was desperately trying to protect.
But more than fear, he felt intense burning excitement in his chest.
I want to climb this tower. Reach the 50th floor as soon as possible.

With his absurd talent, his SSS-rank legendary class, his Divinordial bloodline’s overwhelming advantages, and all his accumulated abilities and powerful cheats, he genuinely believed with complete confidence he could achieve results fast enough to maintain continuous safety. Clear at least one full floor every ten years easily without significant struggle, maintaining the protective grace period indefinitely without ever letting it expire dangerously.
That way, I’ll never have to seriously worry about outside forces threatening my world and all the people living safely here.
Seraphine’s response to his straightforward question about joining him was immediate and incredibly enthusiastic—almost childlike in its eagerness.
She nodded her head repeatedly like an excited puppy, her beautiful amethyst eyes practically sparkling with genuine anticipation and barely contained energy.
She’s been itching for a real fight for so long now. Solo training alone is never the same satisfying experience as actual life-or-death combat against real opponents.

However, after seeing her eager, almost childlike answer, Leon reached out deliberately and patted her head gently with obvious affection. His expression shifted dramatically to something far more serious—almost grave with deep concern.

"Listen carefully, Seraphine. You need to be on absolute high alert at all times inside the tower. Stay close to me constantly throughout everything we encounter, understand? Even though you have the Phoenix Feather resurrection treasure for backup safety, I don’t want to take any unnecessary chances whatsoever with your life."
His tone carried genuine deep concern and intense protectiveness.

Seraphine tilted her head slightly in obvious confusion, her expression clearly showing she didn’t quite understand why he was being so unusually serious and protective about this particular challenge.
She pointed toward the tower’s base foundation area, where Leon had carefully deployed the final purchased item from the cosmic shop.

"But Leon, what about the safety array you specifically told me about before? The Covenant of Stabilized Strife that you deployed specifically for the protection of people while challenging the tower? Doesn’t that prevent permanent death inside?"
Her voice carried genuine curiosity and reasonable logic.
Leon heard her perfectly reasonable question, and while continuing to pat her head affectionately with gentle motions, he shook his head with genuine, visible regret.
"That trick won’t work inside the tower itself. The array is completely useless here."
His voice carried real disappointment at that significant limitation.
I wish it worked. It would make everything safer.
Seraphine’s expression became noticeably more solemn and serious upon hearing that critical safety information. She nodded with understanding gravity.
"I understand completely now. I promise I’ll be as careful as possible. I won’t take unnecessary risks."
Her voice carried sincere commitment.

Leon knew instinctively that the safety array wouldn’t work at all inside the tower—he could tell just by looking at it with his administrator awareness, as if the tower itself was directly communicating with him through their mystical bond, telling him what functioned and what didn’t.
That might be one of the privileges of being a low-level administrator. Direct intuitive knowledge about internal rules and mechanics.

However, he was genuinely unsure about whether his clone would be affected the same way by the tower’s internal rules and death mechanics. That was something he’d definitely need to test carefully and verify later when he had proper time for experimentation, as he got no clue from his instinct.
For now, I’ll leave the clone stationed in the outside world for continuous protection.

The clone would continue serving the critically important function of protecting Ira and all the other Pyrrhans in that increasingly unstable realm while his main body was inside the tower completing challenges. It was increasingly strange and deeply suspicious that two powerful archon-ranked beasts had suddenly shown up during the last festival completely unexpectedly, and even the timing of the dimensional rift opening had been highly unusual and unpredictable compared to all previous established patterns over the years.
Something is definitely wrong in that realm. I can feel it.

He’d already noticed the barely concealed concern and worry that Archon Vyrra had displayed just by observing her facial expressions and body language carefully during the festival celebrations. She was clearly worried about something significant and dangerous she wasn’t openly discussing with anyone, including him.
Better to keep active protection in place until I fully understand what’s actually happening there.
Even if two Archon ranked beast appear like last time his clone was enough to handle one so he was not worried.

Now Leon reached out deliberately and took Seraphine’s hand firmly in his own, interlacing their fingers together securely so they wouldn’t be accidentally separated during transition. He nodded to her with determined resolve.
"Ready?"
"Always," she replied with a confident, beautiful smile that lit up her entire face.
Holding her hand securely so they would remain together, they both stepped forward in unison toward the shining blue gate of the Ascension Tower.
SHIMMER! DISSOLVE!

The moment they made direct physical contact with the portal’s swirling energy, their physical forms seemed to dissolve completely into particles of pure light, vanishing entirely from the dimensional realm’s exterior world.
WHOOSH!
Golden text appeared before them as they transitioned:
[Welcome to the Ascension Tower]
