The 50th floor was specifically and explicitly described as the "true beginning" of the tower system—a gateway floor where countless different worlds, which contained their own individual Ascension Towers, would suddenly connect together, allowing people from completely different civilizations and realms to traverse between worlds and interact directly with each other inside the tower and even outside.
That floor opens everything up completely.
Incredible opportunity for growth, resources, knowledge...
But also tremendous risk of invasion, conflict, and destruction.

Once that critical floor was cleared, powerful hostile forces from other advanced worlds could potentially infiltrate his dimensional realm through the tower connection without facing significant barriers to entry.
However, there was a grace period built carefully into the system—a protective buffer mechanism to prevent immediate catastrophe.
Ten years.
That’s the critical time limit I have to remember.
If he failed to clear another floor within ten years after reaching any major milestone, anyone from connected worlds could infiltrate his realm without any restrictions whatsoever.
But before reaching that dangerous threshold point, without his explicit permission as the tower’s administrator, absolutely no one could enter his world through his specific tower gateway.

Leon felt a genuine spike of fear considering that nightmare scenario playing out—hostile forces from technologically or magically advanced civilizations pouring endlessly into his realm, threatening and killing everyone he was desperately trying to protect.
But more than fear, he felt intense burning excitement in his chest.
I want to climb this tower.
Reach the 50th floor as soon as possible.

With his absurd talent, his SSS-rank legendary class, his Divinordial bloodline’s overwhelming advantages, and all his accumulated abilities and powerful cheats, he genuinely believed with complete confidence he could achieve results fast enough to maintain continuous safety.
Clear at least one full floor every ten years easily without significant struggle, maintaining the protective grace period indefinitely without ever letting it expire dangerously.
That way, I’ll never have to seriously worry about outside forces threatening my world and all the people living safely here.
Seraphine’s response to his straightforward question about joining him was immediate and incredibly enthusiastic—almost childlike in its eagerness.
She nodded her head repeatedly like an excited puppy, her beautiful amethyst eyes practically sparkling with genuine anticipation and barely contained energy.
She’s been itching for a real fight for so long now.
Solo training alone is never the same satisfying experience as actual life-or-death combat against real opponents.
However, after seeing her eager, almost childlike answer, Leon reached out deliberately and patted her head gently with obvious affection.
His expression shifted dramatically to something far more serious—almost grave with deep concern.
"Listen carefully, Seraphine.
You need to be on absolute high alert at all times inside the tower.
Stay close to me constantly throughout everything we encounter, understand?
Even though you have the Phoenix Feather resurrection treasure for backup safety, I don’t want to take any unnecessary chances whatsoever with your life."
His tone carried genuine deep concern and intense protectiveness.

Seraphine tilted her head slightly in obvious confusion, her expression clearly showing she didn’t quite understand why he was being so unusually serious and protective about this particular challenge.
She pointed toward the tower’s base foundation area, where Leon had carefully deployed the final purchased item from the cosmic shop.
"But Leon, what about the safety array you specifically told me about before?
The Covenant of Stabilized Strife that you deployed specifically for the protection of people while challenging the tower?
Doesn’t that prevent permanent death inside?"
Her voice carried genuine curiosity and reasonable logic.
Leon heard her perfectly reasonable question, and while continuing to pat her head affectionately with gentle motions, he shook his head with genuine, visible regret.
"That trick won’t work inside the tower itself.
The array is completely useless here."
His voice carried real disappointment at that significant limitation.
I wish it worked.
It would make everything safer.
Seraphine’s expression became noticeably more solemn and serious upon hearing that critical safety information.
She nodded with understanding gravity.
"I understand completely now.
I promise I’ll be as careful as possible.
I won’t take unnecessary risks."
Her voice carried sincere commitment.

Leon knew instinctively that the safety array wouldn’t work at all inside the tower—he could tell just by looking at it with his administrator awareness, as if the tower itself was directly communicating with him through their mystical bond, telling him what functioned and what didn’t.
That might be one of the privileges of being a low-level administrator.
Direct intuitive knowledge about internal rules and mechanics.
However, he was genuinely unsure about whether his clone would be affected the same way by the tower’s internal rules and death mechanics.
That was something he’d definitely need to test carefully and verify later when he had proper time for experimentation, as he got no clue from his instinct.
For now, I’ll leave the clone stationed in the outside world for continuous protection.

The clone would continue serving the critically important function of protecting Ira and all the other Pyrrhans in that increasingly unstable realm while his main body was inside the tower completing challenges.

It was increasingly strange and deeply suspicious that two powerful archon-ranked beasts had suddenly shown up during the last festival completely unexpectedly, and even the timing of the dimensional rift opening had been highly unusual and unpredictable compared to all previous established patterns over the years.
Something is definitely wrong in that realm.
I can feel it.
He’d already noticed the barely concealed concern and worry that Archon Vyrra had displayed just by observing her facial expressions and body language carefully during the festival celebrations.
She was clearly worried about something significant and dangerous she wasn’t openly discussing with anyone, including him.
Better to keep active protection in place until I fully understand what’s actually happening there.
Even if two Archon ranked beast appear like last time his clone was enough to handle one so he was not worried.
Now Leon reached out deliberately and took Seraphine’s hand firmly in his own, interlacing their fingers together securely so they wouldn’t be accidentally separated during transition.
He nodded to her with determined resolve.
"Ready?"
"Always," she replied with a confident, beautiful smile that lit up her entire face.
Holding her hand securely so they would remain together, they both stepped forward in unison toward the shining blue gate of the Ascension Tower.
SHIMMER!
DISSOLVE!

The moment they made direct physical contact with the portal’s swirling energy, their physical forms seemed to dissolve completely into particles of pure light, vanishing entirely from the dimensional realm’s exterior world.
WHOOSH!
Golden text appeared before them as they transitioned:
[Welcome to the Ascension Tower]

chapters.title: Chapter 428: First Hurdle in the Tower
paragraphs: In the next moment, both Leon and Seraphine found themselves plunged into complete, blinding darkness—an absolute void where neither light nor sound existed.

Leon couldn’t sense Seraphine anywhere despite knowing she’d entered with him just seconds ago. His spatial awareness, usually so reliable and precise, detected nothing but empty black space surrounding him on all sides.
Strange. Where is she? We entered together.
Before he could worry further about their separation, golden text materialized before him in the darkness:
[Select Your Tower Designation Name]
[This name will be your identity within all tower challenges]
[Choose carefully - this cannot be changed]
A nickname? For the tower challenges?
Leon thought for only a moment before making his decision.
"Paragon."

The name was derived directly from his Class—Elemental Paragon—but he deliberately didn’t choose the full title. That complete information might be used against him later or prove seriously disadvantageous if the wrong people learned about his exact class designation.
Better safe than sorry. No reason to broadcast everything about myself to potential enemies.
The system accepted his choice immediately without question:
[Tower Designation Confirmed: Paragon]
[This name will be displayed on all tower records and leaderboards]
Somewhere else in the same dark void—completely separated from Leon—Seraphine was going through an identical process.
She simply chose her usual name without overthinking the decision. Seraphine was who she was, and she saw absolutely no reason to hide her identity for tower challenges.
I have nothing to be ashamed of. My name is my dear disciple, call me so lovingly.
She couldn’t sense Leon anywhere in this strange, isolated space either, which worried her considerably. The separation felt wrong, unnatural.
I hope we’re not separated when we actually enter the first floor proper. We should face these challenges together.
She wasn’t the only one thinking exactly that same thought.
Leon’s mind had reached the identical concerned conclusion about their potential separation during actual trials.
However, just as that worried thought formed clearly and distinctly in his mind—
[Administrator Privilege Detected]
[Special Ability Unlocked: Party Formation System]
[This privilege allows party formation even before the standard required threshold of Floor 10]
[You may invite other challengers to join your party for cooperative trials]
Leon, still floating in the dark void space, couldn’t help but smile with genuine relief seeing that notification appear.
Perfect! So we can stay together after all. The administrator status has real benefits.
He immediately tried to form a party with Seraphine, sending the mental command through the system interface with focused intention.
However, his attempt was instantly and harshly denied with a system message that flashed red:
[Party Formation Request DENIED]
[Reason: The nature of the First Floor Trial does not permit party formation under any circumstances]
[All challengers must complete Floor 1 individually, regardless of privileges or status.]
[This restriction cannot be overridden]
Leon felt disappointment and renewed worry wash through him like cold water.
Damn it. We’re going to be separated after all. No exceptions.

But he could only accept the situation and give up on the party formation idea for now. He had genuine trust and complete faith in Seraphine’s considerable abilities—she would clear the first floor without significant difficulty.
She’s already at Sage rank in terms of cultivation level. That’s genuinely impressive by any standard.

Not only that, she’s a dual elemental user with extremely high affinity in both lightning and light elements. Even in higher-tier worlds with more advanced cultivation standards and stronger competition, she would definitely be considered an exceptional talent.

He’d learned that much from reading the detailed biography of that man of culture, Lin Fan, which had contained comprehensive information about various power hierarchies and what constituted true talent across different worlds.
After the naming process finished completely for both of them—
SHIMMER! VANISH!
They both disappeared from the dark void space simultaneously, transported somewhere else entirely through mechanisms Leon couldn’t perceive.
When Leon’s eyes opened again, he found himself standing inside a massive arena structure.

The space was perfectly circular, maybe two hundred meters in diameter, with smooth, polished stone floors that reflected light like mirrors. High walls seemed to stretch impossibly upward into complete darkness overhead—no visible ceiling existed.
In front of him, floating casually in the air about fifty meters away, was only one figure.
Leon couldn’t gauge the strength of the individual in front of him at all—not even remotely. His finely-tuned instincts, usually so reliable for assessing threats, gave him absolutely nothing useful.

The figure was a man dressed in an immaculate white suit that seemed to be made of some material that shifted and shimmered with movement. He had striking purple hair that fell elegantly to his shoulders in perfectly maintained waves. Purple fur-covered ears protruded from the top of his head, twitching occasionally. A long purple tail swished lazily behind him with predatory grace.
Not human. Definitely a beastfolk from my knowledge of different species encountered so far.

The critical question racing through Leon’s enhanced mind was simple but vital: was this person really weak to the point of being completely beneath his detection threshold, or were they so unfathomably powerful that his senses couldn’t even begin to register their true Level?
Leon’s golden Divinordial heart gave him the answer immediately—it pounded with instinctive warning, beating faster than normal.
The latter. Definitely the latter. This person is monstrously, incomprehensibly strong.

The beastfolk man was looking at him lazily with half-lidded eyes, not saying anything initially. But those purple eyes carried a distinct, unmistakable hint of disdain—an expression of someone looking down at an insect crawling beneath their notice.
Leon didn’t like that condescending expression one bit at all, but he didn’t act rashly or let his anger show on his face.
Instead, he calmly activated his cosmic system’s identification function to check the man’s status and abilities—information that should be accessible.
However, the only piece of information he could actually see was the name displayed at the top:
[Velrith Moonscar]
Everything else— Age, level, Class, stats, skills, abilities, affinities—all appeared as question marks:
[Age: ???] [Level: ???] [Class: ???] [Cultivation Rank: ???] [Stats: ???] [Abilities: ???]
The very instant Leon finished that attempted probe—
FLASH!
The beastfolk’s purple eyes suddenly flashed with a strange ripple of energy that lasted only a millisecond before returning to their previous calm, expressionless state.
The obvious disdain disappeared entirely from his features, replaced now by something far more calculating and interested.
A knowing smirk slowly appeared on his face.
Shit!
Leon realized immediately he’d made a critical tactical mistake. The man had clearly detected his probing attempt despite the cosmic system’s supposedly completely undetectable nature.
How? The system should be invisible to others!
He tensed his entire body, raising his mental and physical guard to maximum alertness, ready to react to any threat.
Then a smooth, cultured voice spoke—carrying an unmistakable undertone of superiority and arrogance.

"I had initially thought a lower world filth had somehow stumbled into this sacred tower in its pitiful ambition or pathetic greed, completely ignorant of the true immensity of heaven and the genuine dangers that await the unworthy."
The beastfolk paused deliberately, his smirk widening with satisfaction.
"But it seems I was quite mistaken about certain... aspects of your situation."
He had clearly made some private conclusion in his mind based on whatever he’d detected or sensed from Leon’s probing attempt, but he didn’t voice those specific thoughts aloud.
Instead, he introduced himself with formal precision.
"I am Velrith Moonscar, mid-level administrator of this Ascension Tower and the one who will be personally conducting your trial evaluation today... Mister Paragon."

chapters.title: Chapter 429: First Hurdle in the Tower—2
paragraphs: "I am Velrith Moonscar, mid-level administrator of this Ascension Tower and the one who will be personally conducting your trial evaluation today... Mister Paragon."
His tone dripped with obvious amusement on that last part, as if the name itself was a joke.
"What a remarkably bold name you’ve chosen for yourself. Quite... presumptuous and arrogant for someone of your obviously humble origins."
He was clearly looking for a reaction, trying deliberately to provoke Leon into revealing something through anger or pride.
But Leon kept his guard up at all times, maintaining his expression carefully neutral despite the blatant condescension and insults.
Velrith smiled slightly at the lack of visible reaction, seemingly pleased by Leon’s control.
Then he descended from his floating position without warning.
WHOOSH!
In an instant—not through spatial teleportation but through pure, overwhelming physical speed that Leon’s eyes could barely track—Velrith appeared directly next to him, less than a meter away.

Leon could only flinch reflexively when the man had already arrived right in front of him. His body moved on pure instinct, immediately backing off several quick steps to create distance and defensive space.
"Relax, human," Velrith said casually, waving a dismissive hand. "I’m not going to harm you."
Yet, his amused eyes seemed to silently add.
But Leon kept his guard up regardless of the reassurance, not trusting a single word from this obviously condescending and potentially hostile creature.
Actions speak louder than words. And his actions show superiority and disdain.

Velrith’s smile widened slightly at Leon’s continued wariness and refusal to relax. Then he reached out with one elegant hand and took something from apparently thin air—clearly pulling an item from a high-quality spatial storage artifact.
Leon’s eyes immediately locked onto the object with focused attention.

It was an extraordinarily luxurious bottle, clearly made of some form of crystallized mana or precious material. Inside swirled a shimmering liquid that seemed to shift fluidly through multiple vibrant colors—deep red, brilliant blue, radiant gold, pure silver—in mesmerizing, hypnotic patterns.
Leon could tell instantly it was something genuinely extraordinary just from the powerful ambient energy it radiated, even while contained.
Suddenly, without him even attempting to identify it, detailed information appeared floating in golden text directly in front of him:
[Prismatic Awakening Elixir]
[Rarity: Legendary]
[Primary Effect: Permanently increases ALL physical and mental stats by exactly 100 points]
[Secondary Effect: Awakens one random Rank 6 elemental affinity in the consumer]
[Note: Affinity awakened will be completely random - cannot be selected or influenced]
[Value: Immeasurable - Wars have been fought over lesser treasures in certain worlds]
This was an incredibly, extraordinarily valuable item!
Leon’s eyes gleamed involuntarily, seeing those powerful effects listed so clearly.
With this, Seraphine would become so much stronger immediately...

The first trial separation had made him realize with absolute crystal clarity how critically important it was for Seraphine to become even more powerful independently—to develop into a genuine powerhouse in her own right rather than someone who constantly needed his protection.

For that ultimate goal, he’d already made the firm decision that she would soon undergo her class reawakening process, which would make her significantly stronger than her current already-impressive state.

And this particular item would make her vastly better prepared when taking future dangerous trials. Having three distinct elemental affinities instead of just two would provide an enormous tactical and power advantage.
Three elements to combine and utilize. The versatility alone would be incredible.
The trial overseer observed Leon’s facial expression carefully with predatory interest, clearly seeing the obvious desire and interest written across the human’s features.
He chuckled slightly, the sound carrying deep satisfaction.
"You recognize quality when you see it. Good. You can have this item, human. Take it with my blessing."
He paused deliberately for effect.
"All you need to do is answer one simple, straightforward question of mine. That’s all I ask."
Hearing that seemingly generous offer, Leon kept his complete silence, his wariness increasing dramatically.
Nothing is ever free, especially from someone like this.
The overseer simply proceeded with his question anyway, despite the lack of response, his voice carrying unmistakable pride and superiority.

"This elixir is something that even among people of my Level and exalted status is desperately coveted and fought over. Despite the affinity awakening being ’only’ Rank 6, it’s still an additional complete affinity—something absolutely worth killing for in most circumstances."
He paused for dramatic emphasis, letting that sink in.

"Rank 7 affinity elixirs are legendary items that entire powerful factions and ancient clans wage prolonged wars to obtain even a single dose. Even these Rank 6 versions are extraordinarily difficult to acquire through any means, depending on the specific affinity involved and market availability."
Rank 7, there are items that can awaken rank 7 affinity out there!! Leon thought greedily, flashing his eyes, and from the way it seemed, both these items are extremely valuable.
His purple eyes focused intently on Leon with laser precision.
"So tell me, human. Answer this one simple question, and all of this is yours."
Another deliberate pause.
"How does a human from an obviously lower world, with cultivation at merely Ascendant rank, somehow possess a higher-grade cosmic system?"
The question hung in the air between them like a suspended blade ready to fall.
Leon’s expression didn’t change externally, but internally, his mind raced at incredible speed.
So that’s what he detected when I probed him. He knows I have a higher-grade system than normal. How much does he actually know?
The overseer continued speaking, his tone becoming increasingly curious and hungry for information.

"It’s completely unprecedented in all my considerable experience and knowledge. Absolutely unheard of. I attempted to check your basic status information, but for some utterly incomprehensible reason, I cannot even perceive your name, which is absolutely absurd given our massive level difference."
Velrith’s eyes narrowed slightly with genuine confusion and frustration.

"I can tell you’re at Ascendant rank cultivation—that much is obvious. But the secrets you hold are clearly heaven-defying in nature. Are you perhaps some ancient, powerful being’s carefully planned reincarnation? Even that extreme explanation doesn’t adequately explain how you possess a cosmic system of that apparent grade."
He leaned forward slightly, intense interest radiating from his entire posture.

"Or why I—someone more than one hundred full levels higher than your current pathetic rank—cannot probe even your most basic information like name. Your Class and affinity could theoretically be hidden from detection since I also possess a higher-grade cosmic system myself. But your physical stats, your skills, your name, your Age, your race details—everything? That should be completely impossible through any known method."
The beastfolk’s smile turned distinctly predatory, showing hints of sharp fangs.

"I cannot let this fascinating mystery go unanswered and unexplored. This secret alone—whatever method you’re using—would allow me to earn rewards and recognition worth vastly more than this measly elixir, valuable as it is."
Leon thought for only a brief moment, then spoke clearly and firmly.
"I decline your offer entirely."
His voice was hard, carrying absolutely no hesitation whatsoever.

With enough causality accumulated over time, I can buy items matching this effect or even higher quality directly from the cosmic shop. Or I can obtain similar powerful rewards by climbing the Tower itself and completing challenges, which is almost certainly how this overseer obtained that elixir in the first place.
Leon doesn’t know that for normal people, even those who had become immortal, the number of casualties was too much.
Earning causality was not such an easy task.
But who can tell him that when he was scamming higher being who can erase his world with their fart alone, well if they knew about it.

The overseer simply proceeded with his question anyway, despite the lack of response, his voice carrying unmistakable pride and superiority.
"This elixir is something that even among people of my Level and exalted status is desperately coveted and fought over.
Despite the affinity awakening being ’only’ Rank 6, it’s still an additional complete affinity—something absolutely worth killing for in most circumstances."
He paused for dramatic emphasis, letting that sink in.
"Rank 7 affinity elixirs are legendary items that entire powerful factions and ancient clans wage prolonged wars to obtain even a single dose.
Even these Rank 6 versions are extraordinarily difficult to acquire through any means, depending on the specific affinity involved and market availability."
Rank 7, there are items that can awaken rank 7 affinity out there!!
Leon thought greedily, flashing his eyes, and from the way it seemed, both these items are extremely valuable.
His purple eyes focused intently on Leon with laser precision.
"So tell me, human.
Answer this one simple question, and all of this is yours."
Another deliberate pause.
"How does a human from an obviously lower world, with cultivation at merely Ascendant rank, somehow possess a higher-grade cosmic system?"
The question hung in the air between them like a suspended blade ready to fall.
Leon’s expression didn’t change externally, but internally, his mind raced at incredible speed.
So that’s what he detected when I probed him.
He knows I have a higher-grade system than normal.
How much does he actually know?
The overseer continued speaking, his tone becoming increasingly curious and hungry for information.
"It’s completely unprecedented in all my considerable experience and knowledge.
Absolutely unheard of.
I attempted to check your basic status information, but for some utterly incomprehensible reason, I cannot even perceive your name, which is absolutely absurd given our massive level difference."
Velrith’s eyes narrowed slightly with genuine confusion and frustration.
"I can tell you’re at Ascendant rank cultivation—that much is obvious.
But the secrets you hold are clearly heaven-defying in nature.
Are you perhaps some ancient, powerful being’s carefully planned reincarnation?
Even that extreme explanation doesn’t adequately explain how you possess a cosmic system of that apparent grade."
He leaned forward slightly, intense interest radiating from his entire posture.
"Or why I—someone more than one hundred full levels higher than your current pathetic rank—cannot probe even your most basic information like name.
Your Class and affinity could theoretically be hidden from detection since I also possess a higher-grade cosmic system myself.
But your physical stats, your skills, your name, your Age, your race details—everything?
That should be completely impossible through any known method."
The beastfolk’s smile turned distinctly predatory, showing hints of sharp fangs.
"I cannot let this fascinating mystery go unanswered and unexplored.
This secret alone—whatever method you’re using—would allow me to earn rewards and recognition worth vastly more than this measly elixir, valuable as it is."
Leon thought for only a brief moment, then spoke clearly and firmly.
"I decline your offer entirely."
His voice was hard, carrying absolutely no hesitation whatsoever.
With enough causality accumulated over time, I can buy items matching this effect or even higher quality directly from the cosmic shop.
Or I can obtain similar powerful rewards by climbing the Tower itself and completing challenges, which is almost certainly how this overseer obtained that elixir in the first place.
Leon doesn’t know that for normal people, even those who had become immortal, the number of casualties was too much.
Earning causality was not such an easy task.
But who can tell him that when he was scamming higher being who can erase his world with their fart alone, well if they knew about it.

chapters.title: Chapter 430: First Hurdle in the Tower—3
paragraphs: I absolutely cannot reveal my deepest secrets about my SSS-class and cosmic system grade to anyone, especially not someone like this obviously untrustworthy individual.
The moment Leon clearly rejected the offer—
SNARL!
Velrith’s fangs bared fully for just a millisecond, his carefully maintained civilized mask slipping completely.
CRUSH!
An absolutely insurmountable, overwhelming, heavy pressure descended on Leon like a physical mountain crushing down from all directions simultaneously.
Leon’s heart dropped sickeningly into his stomach.
I’m going to die! Right here, right now!
The pressure was so catastrophically intense he could barely draw breath into his lungs, his vision tunneling dangerously, consciousness threatening to scatter.
But in the very next second—
RELEASE!
The pressure vanished completely and instantly as if it had never existed at all.
Velrith was smiling pleasantly again, his expression perfectly composed and friendly.
"My sincere apologies, human. I lost control of my aura for a brief moment there. No harm intended whatsoever, of course. These things happen occasionally."
But Leon had learned something absolutely critical from that terrifying exchange.
He can’t actually harm me directly. The Tower’s rules prevent it completely.
That realization made him considerably more relaxed internally, though he remained outwardly cautious.
If he could actually harm me without restriction, I’d be dead already or being tortured for information right now. The Tower protects challengers from administrators.
Over the next several minutes, Velrith produced various other spectacular items from his spatial storage with increasing desperation.
Legendary weapons that radiated absolutely terrifying, destructive power—swords that seemed to cut through space itself, spears that hummed with condensed lightning.
Armor sets that appeared to be made of pure condensed starlight, shimmering with protective enchantments.
Mysterious treasures that pulsed with ancient primordial energies, Leon couldn’t even begin to identify or understand.
Each item was demonstrably no lesser in objective value than the initial elixir—some were arguably even significantly more valuable depending on specific needs.
And Leon refused every single offer without hesitation, his answer consistent.
"I decline."
"Not interested."
"No."
After the first rejection, Velrith maintained a perfectly calm exterior—serene and composed as a still mountain lake.

But Leon could read the absolute truth in his eyes despite the false smile. Inside, the overseer desperately wanted to torture him brutally for the information he sought, growing progressively more frustrated and enraged with each successive refusal.
The trial overseer was genuinely fuming internally with barely controlled rage.
No matter what this human’s background or special circumstances might be, right now he’s just a measly insect—barely Ascendant rank! Nothing!
And despite my clear seniority, my obvious power, and these incredibly generous offers, the arrogant bastard keeps rejecting me again and again!
Unacceptable! Intolerable!
Finally, after all the individual item offers had been systematically rejected, Velrith made his absolute final offer with complete apparent seriousness.

A golden parchment materialized from thin air, floating majestically in the space between them. An elaborate contract written in flowing divine script that seemed to shift and reorganize itself slightly as Leon examined it.
The details were extensive, comprehensive, and incredibly generous:
SOUL-BINDING CONTRACT OF MUTUAL BENEFIT
TERMS AND CONDITIONS:
Article I - Guidance and Support
Velrith Moonscar shall personally guide the Contractee (designated: Paragon) through all challenges up to Floor 100 of the Ascension Tower.
Provide strategic advice, tactical recommendations, and reveal all hidden bosses, secret treasures, and optimal challenge approaches.
Article II - Protection Services
Use all available administrative authority to protect the Contractee’s home world from invasions by connected worlds
Provide early warning and direct intervention against external threats when possible, within tower rules
Maintain protection for the full duration of the Contractee’s tower climbing journey
Article III - Resource Provision
Grant access to restricted administrator treasure vaults (Floors 1-50)
Provide monthly cultivation resources scaled to the current Level
Share advanced techniques from Velrith’s personal collection
Article IV - Post-Contract Obligations After contract expiration, Velrith shall:
Never directly or indirectly harm the Contractee or anyone/anything connected to them
Never reveal the Contractee’s secrets, identity, abilities, or existence to any party
Never take action hostile to the Contractee’s interests
Article V - Consideration In exchange for the above services, the Contractee shall:
Truthfully explain the method of concealing status information from higher-level beings
Reveal how a lower-world individual obtained a higher-grade cosmic system
Share any relevant techniques, items, or methods enabling these effects
ENFORCEMENT: Bound by Laws of Heaven and enforced by the Tower. Violation results in immediate soul destruction. No loopholes exist.
DURATION: Until Contractee reaches Floor 100, withdraws permanently, or dies outside tower trials.
Leon read the entire contract carefully multiple times, examining every single clause with his enhanced intelligence, analyzing each word for hidden meanings.
There are genuinely no loopholes. The contract is absolutely ironclad. The Tower itself enforces it with soul destruction as a penalty. And the offer is... incredibly, almost unbelievably enticing.
For a long moment—several full minutes—Leon genuinely considered accepting this proposal.
The benefits are enormous. Complete guidance through one hundred floors. Protection for my world. Resources and techniques. And absolute guarantees he can’t harm me afterward.
All for just explaining my status concealment method and system grade origin.
Meanwhile, Velrith was thinking with absolute unshakeable confidence.

Despite this offer putting an absolutely enormous hole in my accumulated resources and requiring me to sacrifice treasures I’ve collected over centuries, the secret alone—the method to completely hide one’s status information from even vastly higher-level beings—would make me a fortune one hundred times this investment.
Possibly even a thousand times. Such a technique could revolutionize assassination, espionage, and infiltration. Every major power would pay anything for it.
He was completely confident this human couldn’t possibly reject this extraordinarily generous offer.
Who would? Even if I were in his exact position, I would accept this offer without hesitation. No hidden strings, complete protection, full support for reaching a level where one can be independent.
He knew his earlier theatrical display of disdain, condescension, and applying that brief pressure had put the human significantly on edge and defensive.
So this contract offer was completely, genuinely sincere—he honestly wanted what was truly best for both of them. A mutually beneficial arrangement.
We both win. I get the secret. He gets support to reach heights he could never achieve alone. Perfect.
Leon’s mouth finally opened after his long contemplation, his eyes gleaming with what Velrith interpreted as excitement and acceptance.
Velrith leaned forward slightly in eager anticipation, ready to finalize the contract.
"I refuse."
The words were clear, firm, and absolutely final.
The overseer’s entire body trembled violently with pure, unrestrained rage.
His eyes became completely bloodshot, pupils dilating into narrow slits.
THIS WAS MY FULL SINCERITY! EVERYTHING I HAVE OF VALUE! CENTURIES OF ACCUMULATED WEALTH!
Multiple revival treasures are worth kingdoms! Rank 6 affinity potions that clans war over! Even the Rank 6 Poison Affinity Awakening Potion I was planning to trade for the Celestial Flame Seed!

That poison affinity potion specifically didn’t suit his lightning-based fighting style at all, and his clan would genuinely look down on any member using poison-based techniques—it was considered dishonorable.

Even his own clan head didn’t know Velrith possessed such an incredibly valuable item. He’d been secretly saving it for years to trade for something he desperately wanted for his cultivation breakthrough.
And this... this INSECT rejected everything! Rejected an offer that would make any rational person weep with joy!
Velrith was enraged beyond all measure, beyond anything he’d felt in decades.

He knew intellectually he couldn’t harm this human directly due to tower rules protecting active challengers. And from the human’s noticeably more relaxed posture compared to earlier, it was obvious Leon had also realized that protective fact.
Which somehow infuriated Velrith even more.
He knows he’s safe. He’s mocking me with his refusals!

chapters.title: Chapter 431: First Hurdle in the Tower—4
paragraphs: The negotiation was completely over. Velrith just wanted to see this arrogant worm suffer eventually.
His fangs protruded fully, all pretense of civility and politeness utterly abandoned.
The overseer sneered with a genuinely murderous expression that promised future violence, openly throwing explicit threats.

"You have overstepped your bounds tremendously, you filthy lower-world human! Just you wait patiently—sooner or later, I will discover your precious secret! You cannot hide from me forever behind these restrictive tower rules!"
His voice lowered to a threatening growl filled with malice.

"After I find out exactly what makes you so special and unique, I will slowly, methodically kill you using the most painful methods I know. Along with everyone you know and care about. Your family, your lovers, your friends—all dead."
His smile turned absolutely vicious.
"Your entire filthy world will burn to ashes. Every single living thing on it will scream before they die. And I’ll make sure you watch every moment before I finally end you."
Then, as if a switch had been flipped instantly, his fangs retracted completely, and his expression became pleasant and friendly again—as if those horrific threats had never been spoken at all.
"Now then. This is your very last chance, human. Sign this generous contract to save yourself and your filthy world from the inevitable future consequences of your arrogance."

Administrator was sure that threat would work at very least, he didn’t want to go that far, but it had come to this, it doesn’t matter if he was a reincarnation of some powerful being, right now he was an ant before him.
Those specific words made Leon genuinely afraid. Yes, he was terrified hearing such detailed, explicit threats from a being of such overwhelming power who clearly meant every word.
He could actually do all of that once the Tower rules no longer protect me. Destroy everything I’m trying to build and protect.
But more than fear, far stronger than terror, he felt absolutely burning rage.
How DARE he threaten my life! Threaten the people precious to me!

Vivid images flashed rapidly through his mind—Seraphine’s beautiful smile, the awakened humans trusting him completely with their lives, Ira’s fierce, devoted love, Archon Vrya’s determined devotion to save her people, everyone depending on him for protection and safety.
Leon knew rationally it would be incredibly difficult and dangerous after reaching the 50th floor and connecting to countless other worlds filled with powerful beings.
But in that precise moment, staring at this arrogant creature, he made an absolute iron resolution.
I’m going to kill this worm. Sooner or later, he’s dead by my hand. I don’t care how long it takes.
Instead of cowering before the threats like Velrith clearly expected, Leon felt his resolve to grow stronger crystallize into diamond-hard determination that nothing could shake.

For the first time in his entire life across both existences, his desire to gain power burned hotter than it ever had before—fueled not just by ambition or survival instinct, but by pure hatred and the overwhelming need to protect what truly mattered.
The overseer’s threats fell on ears that acted completely deaf to intimidation.
Leon answered not with fear or submission, but with cold, absolute resolve and completely undisguised hatred toward the creature he would eventually destroy.

Unconsciously, without even realizing it, he activated Leximancy—his spatial trait ability that he’d never properly focused on developing before, a subtle power that infused his spoken words with reality-warping force.
"Start the trial, you worm."
Those five words hit the trial overseer like an actual physical blow to his ear.
This INSECT HOW DARE HE!!!

For a brief moment, Velrith actually paused mid-breath—not because of any external binding force, but because he felt a strange, completely unexpected ripple pass directly across his soul itself, it doesn’t
Was that... an attack? Did this insect just attack my soul with words?
It didn’t do anything, but he felt it on his soul.

The tower rules still bound him completely from retaliating since it hadn’t been registered or considered a direct attack by the Tower. But to affect the soul—even on just a molecular level—of a being so much higher in cultivation with mere spoken words?
Is it a legendary artifact? Some soul-bound treasure? Or... something else entirely? Another secret this human possesses?
His burning resolve to obtain this human’s secrets increased exponentially to the point of obsession.
And the fact this lowly insect actually called ME—Velrith Moonscar of the Purple Moon Clan—a worm...

Velrith decided with absolute finality in that instant: even if Leon had signed the contract and revealed everything, he would have completely destroyed the human world anyway and brutally killed everyone remotely related to him, purely for the profound disrespect and insult.
No one calls me a worm. NO ONE! not even the Clan head!!
But the tower rules bound him absolutely to proceed with the trial explanation as required by protocol.
Through gritted teeth hidden behind a false smile, Velrith began explaining in a deliberately monotone voice, speaking as quickly as rules allowed.

Leon listened with a cold, emotionless heart, his mind already racing ahead to intensive thoughts of how to get dramatically stronger as quickly as possible—what type of absolutely brutal training regimen he should implement when he returned outside.
I need power. Real power. Enough to crush beings like this eventually.
The trial structure was straightforward and simple:
He had to defeat opponents that would materialize and attack him in successive waves. Depending on how many stages he successfully cleared, he would receive rewards befitting that achievement level.

He could choose to give up and exit the trial mid-way, but only after clearing at least the first stage completely. Before that critical threshold, it was either complete victory or permanent death—no middle ground, no escape.
After finishing the mandatory explanation as required by tower protocol, Velrith asked with barely concealed hatred dripping from every word:
"Are you ready to begin, worm?"
He deliberately used Leon’s insult back, his voice promising future suffering.
Leon only nodded coldly, his expression carved from absolute ice.
His hand moved with practiced precision, and his sword materialized instantly in his grip—the blade gleaming with barely suppressed holy power.
Right after that confirmation—
FLASH!
An intense blue light formed at the opposite end of the large arena, maybe a hundred and fifty meters away. The light coalesced rapidly into the distinct shape of a small bipedal creature.
Within just a few seconds, it fully materialized into solid form.
A green-skinned creature stood there, noticeably smaller than Leon—maybe only chest height at most. It gripped a crude iron sword in one clawed hand, the weapon looking primitive but functional.
A goblin.
Leon recognized it immediately at first glance from his accumulated knowledge of monster types and classifications.
But he absolutely didn’t let his guard down despite its relatively small size and seemingly weak appearance.
Size means nothing. Cultivation rank is everything.
He immediately checked its status with his system:
[Trial Goblin - Ascendant Rank]
Same exact rank as me. And no other useful information is available.
Leon settled smoothly into a ready combat stance, his muscles coiled like compressed springs ready to explode into action.
His holy energy reserves churned powerfully inside him, ready to burst forth at any moment he commanded.
The goblin’s glowing red eyes locked onto Leon with predatory focus, and it released a piercing, ear-splitting shriek.
SCREEE!
Then it charged forward with surprising explosive speed, covering ground far faster than its small legs should allow.

Within just a few seconds, it fully materialized into solid form.
A green-skinned creature stood there, noticeably smaller than Leon—maybe only chest height at most.
It gripped a crude iron sword in one clawed hand, the weapon looking primitive but functional.
A goblin.
Leon recognized it immediately at first glance from his accumulated knowledge of monster types and classifications.
But he absolutely didn’t let his guard down despite its relatively small size and seemingly weak appearance.
Size means nothing.
Cultivation rank is everything.
He immediately checked its status with his system:
[Trial Goblin - Ascendant Rank]
Same exact rank as me.
And no other useful information is available.
Leon settled smoothly into a ready combat stance, his muscles coiled like compressed springs ready to explode into action.
His holy energy reserves churned powerfully inside him, ready to burst forth at any moment he commanded.
The goblin’s glowing red eyes locked onto Leon with predatory focus, and it released a piercing, ear-splitting shriek.
SCREEE!
Then it charged forward with surprising explosive speed, covering ground far faster than its small legs should allow.

chapters.title: Chapter 432: First Floor of Ascension Tower
paragraphs: The speed of the charging goblin would have seemed incredibly fast in the eyes of a normal Ascendant rank being—a blur of motion that would require serious reaction time to counter.
However, to Leon, it was painfully, almost insultingly slow.
Like watching someone move through water.
He just stood there calmly with his sword still sheathed in its scabbard, gripped loosely in his right hand. His expression remained completely neutral, almost bored.
The goblin closed the distance rapidly, raising its crude iron sword for a devastating overhead strike aimed at splitting Leon’s skull.
When it was mere meters away, entering optimal striking range—
FLASH!
Leon’s hand moved.

A single slash, drawn and completed in one fluid motion. No flashy skills, no elaborate techniques, no elemental enhancement. Just a perfectly executed normal slash with pure physical power and impeccable form.
SLICE!
The goblin split cleanly in half vertically, its body separating into two perfect halves that fell away from each other.
THUD! THUD!
Both halves hit the ground simultaneously.
Too easy. Far too easy for something supposedly at my rank.
Leon flicked his blade once to remove the blood, then resheathed it smoothly.

High above in the air, watching this entire exchange with increasingly dark eyes, the trial overseer who had already formed a deep, murderous grudge against this impudent human merely scoffed loudly at the display.
Showing off. The arrogant worm is showing off to me specifically.
Velrith’s purple eyes narrowed with intense irritation.

It’s just the first layer of the trial—the absolute easiest threshold. And his nonchalant demeanor, acting as if he’s some one-in-a-million genius from the Celestial Realm rather than lower-world trash.
It just irks me beyond measure.

After killing the creature so effortlessly, Leon received a system message. The familiar transparent golden panel appeared before him, but this time it bore the distinct tower logo behind it—indicating the message originated directly from the Ascension Tower itself rather than his personal cosmic system.
[First Layer Cleared Successfully]
[Trial Completion Time: 3 seconds]
[Evaluation: In Progress]
[You may now choose to withdraw from the trial and claim your current rewards, or proceed to the Second Layer]
[Rest Period Granted: 10 minutes before automatic continuation]
Without even resting for a single second—without so much as taking a deep breath—Leon directly chose to continue immediately to the second layer of the trial.
No reason to delay. I’m not even slightly tired.
Just then, the corpse remains of the defeated goblin began glowing with brilliant white light.
SHIMMER! DISSOLVE!
It completely vanished without leaving any traces whatsoever—not even a speck of blood remained on the pristine arena floor, as if the creature had never existed.
The cleaning mechanism was impressively efficient.
Then, a couple of seconds afterward—
FLASH! FLASH! FLASH!
Ten similar-looking goblins materialized in front of Leon simultaneously, appearing in a rough semicircle formation.

The pressure emanating from their bodies was noticeably much stronger than the first trial monster. Just by observing their sharp, focused gazes and coordinated positioning, one could immediately tell they were fundamentally different from the previous mindless goblin.
However, using his cosmic system’s identification function, Leon could see their basic information clearly:
[Trial Goblin - Ascendant Rank] [Trial Goblin - Ascendant Rank] [Trial Goblin - Ascendant Rank] ...
Still all Ascendant rank according to the system. But clearly enhanced versions.

The moment they fully appeared and solidified, Leon felt distinctly how they enhanced their physical bodies with flowing mana—not crudely but with practiced efficiency. The thin coating of light on their various weapons was unmistakably Level 2 Aura, showing genuine combat mastery.

They immediately surrounded him from all directions with tactical precision, moving into a proper combat formation. Their weapons were notably different and complementary—sword, wand, spear, shield, mace, bow—like a balanced party formation designed for group combat.
Interesting. They’re coordinating like an actual adventuring party.
Leon simply stood there calmly in the center of their formation, not moving to preemptively attack.
Then it began.
WHOOSH! CRACK! BOOM!

A barrage of long-range attacks came flying in his direction from multiple angles simultaneously—fire bolts from the wand-wielder, arrows from the archer, thrown spears, everything converging on his position.
Leon merely mobilized his ice element with minimal effort.
SHIMMER! CRACK!

Thin barriers of crystallized ice materialized in the air around him, intercepting and deflecting every single attack with perfect precision. Not a single projectile touched even a strand of his hair.
He didn’t move even an inch, maintaining his calm expression throughout the onslaught.

However, the goblins didn’t directly charge at him from close range like the first one had done. They kept attacking methodically from distance, maintaining their formation and continuing the barrage.
Smart. They’re testing my defenses first.

Looking into their eyes, Leon could clearly see they possessed intelligence similar to an adult human at the very least. They were deliberately trying to wear him down and exhaust his resources, using their numerical advantage tactically.
They’re treating this like a real battle. Conserving energy, probing for weaknesses, maintaining formation discipline.

Leon didn’t know if, in this evaluation for the first floor, the time taken to defeat enemies affected the final assessment or not. The overseer hadn’t told him anything about scoring criteria—he’d just glossed over the explanation quickly, providing only the bare minimum information needed to understand what had to be done and nothing more.
Deliberately vague. Probably hoping I’d make mistakes from ignorance.
So just to be on the safe side and avoid potentially affecting his evaluation negatively, Leon decided not to waste any more time playing defensive.
Besides, I need to test my current combat capabilities properly.
However, he had to acknowledge that the difficulty jump from the first layer to the second layer went from approximately 1 to 100 immediately—no gradual progression in between whatsoever.
For a normal person with standard talent and training, this level alone would be more than enough for them to wisely give up the challenge and quit here before suffering serious injury or death.
Most people would struggle significantly. Some would die.
However, Leon was extraordinarily far from normal by any reasonable standard.

chapters.title: Chapter 433: First Floor of Ascension Tower—2
paragraphs: Leon didn’t even bother activating his mana body enhancement technique. His physical body—being the Divinordial race and having endured countless tribulations and hellish training—was vastly superior to others at the same cultivation rank.
My body alone is stronger than most people with full enhancement active.
He knew instinctively he didn’t need artificial enhancement for handling these particular foes.
Leon’s gaze sharpened with focused intent.

He unsheathed his sword in one smooth, practiced motion. The blade came free with a distinctive metallic sound, gleaming with a bright blue sheen—though it wasn’t the natural color of the metal itself but rather highly condensed ice elemental energy coating the entire length.
Then he slashed with lightning-fast speed.
Sky Breaker Draw — executed with Transcendent Rank mastery, combined seamlessly with condensed ice element.
SLASH!
An intense blue thread of concentrated ice energy unleashed from his blade, moving far faster than the eye could track.

The attack manifested as razor-thin lines that appeared simultaneously on the bodies of all ten goblins—specifically across their necks with surgical precision. They didn’t even have time to react defensively or attempt to dodge.
All this happened in mere milliseconds.
Thin blue lines appeared across each goblin’s throat, glowing faintly.
Then the icy energy didn’t stop there—it continued traveling through the air, passing through where the goblins stood, and finally collided violently with the reinforced edge of the arena itself.
BOOM! CRACK!
A massive explosion erupted where the attack hit the barrier, sending cracks spider-webbing across the protective formation before it absorbed and dispersed the excess energy.
Back at the goblins’ positions—
FREEZE!
The ten creatures’ necks didn’t simply get cut. Instead, the overwhelming ice energy spread rapidly from the wound points, completely freezing their entire bodies from the inside out within seconds.
Their expressions locked in shock and confusion, unable to comprehend what had just killed them.
SHATTER!
Then they all shattered simultaneously into countless fine ice pieces, like delicate ice sculptures broken by an invisible hammer.
The potency of Leon’s attack was on such a vastly higher level than these trial goblins’ bodies could possibly handle—even after death, the residual ice energy continued destroying them completely.
Watching this display from high above, the overseer felt a strong ripple pass through his purple eyes as a distinctly grim expression appeared on his face for the first time.
No. This can’t be...
Seeing how absurdly easily this human had passed the second layer—which was supposed to be a genuine challenge requiring tactical thinking—made him realize something deeply troubling.
When I took this assessment centuries ago, it wasn’t nearly this smooth. I struggled significantly on the second layer.
The realization hit him like cold water.
This human might actually pass the third layer. Or... may even have a slim possibility to contend with the fourth layer.

Velrith himself had only managed to pass the third layer successfully with a B-level assessment, which had been just good enough for him to be considered a respectable small genius within his prestigious clan.
And now this lower-world insect is performing better than I did?

Realizing that this human—who was now definitely his mortal enemy—possessed even greater natural potential than himself, combined with the fact that he could wield the ice element which was categorized as one of the genuinely uncommon elements...
He’s more special than I initially estimated.

In terms of pure elemental affinity rank, Velrith didn’t feel particularly concerned as of right now. But he knew clearly this wasn’t everything the human had shown so far—there were definitely more hidden cards.

He made a solemn promise to his heart in that moment: the instant this tower connected to the vast network and the protection period officially ended, he would personally come here and methodically destroy this human and his entire planet without mercy. And obtain every single secret he possessed.

The chance of this human actually becoming a genuine threat to me is close to zero despite his potential being somewhat greater than mine. There’s a vast generational difference in cultivation level and social status between us.
Velrith didn’t truly have to be so excessively cautious to begin with. However, extreme caution was precisely why he’d survived this long and achieved his current position of power and authority.
Better to eliminate potential threats before they can grow.
A similar system message appeared in front of Leon’s eyes after the ice pieces finished dissolving:
[Second Layer Cleared Successfully]
[Trial Completion Time: 1.2 seconds]
[Evaluation: In Progress]
[You may now choose to withdraw from the trial and claim your current rewards, or proceed to the Third Layer]
[Rest Period Granted: 10 minutes before automatic continuation]
Leon could choose to continue immediately right away.
However, he then glanced upward at the figure floating high in the air, watching his every move with those calculating purple eyes.
I don’t like this feeling. Being constantly watched by someone who is my mortal enemy—someone I will eventually kill—but who is currently far too strong for me to contend with directly.
He was thinking deeply if there was any possible way he could keep himself and his hidden trump cards away from this bastard’s prying eyes.
The thought of enclosing the entire arena with his Ice Domain ability entered his mind as a potential solution.
However, Leon immediately shook his head right afterward, dismissing the idea.
That wouldn’t be nearly enough. The distance between our power levels is too vast—it wouldn’t work at all against someone at his level.
The overseer gave him that completely unfathomable feeling, like trying to measure an ocean’s depth with a short stick.

As he was feeling genuinely helpless and thinking with regret that he should have saved some causality as emergency funds—there definitely would have been some useful privacy-related treasures available in the cosmic shop that could have helped him in his current scenario—
A sudden unexpected message floated into view directly in front of him, as if the tower itself was sensing his specific thoughts and responding to his will.
[Administrator Privilege Detected]
[Tower suggestion given detection Administrator will]
[Special Option Available: Private Trial Mode]
[Would you like to make your trial evaluation private?]
[Effect: All observers except designated Administrator of the specified Tower itself will be removed from observation Authority of the trial]
[This setting can be activated at any point during trials]
[Confirm?]

chapters.title: Chapter 434: First Floor of Ascension Tower—3
paragraphs: Leon’s eyes widened slightly reading this.
There’s an option to make it private? This is perfect!

This particular feature was something that only people who possessed great backgrounds and extensive knowledge about the Ascension Tower system were aware of—privileged information passed down through powerful families and organizations.
Yet for normal people and those from lower worlds, this was crucial information they typically came to learn about much later in their journey, often after suffering from unwanted attention.

And those high in power and authority deliberately wouldn’t share this knowledge freely. It served as an excellent method to recruit promising individuals into their factions, and also as a tool to keep careful surveillance on upcoming prodigies and geniuses among the masses.
Many of those powerful people had various forms of direct connection with tower administrators and possessed authority to gain access to this kind of classified operational information.
However, Leon was naturally completely unaware of all these complicated political dynamics and hidden implications as of right now.

The simple presence of this hostile overseer—with whom he’d formed what was essentially a life-and-death grudge—gave him the straightforward idea of hiding his secrets and capabilities from the overseer’s observation. Nothing more complex than that.
He didn’t know that by making this choice, he was potentially escaping from unimaginable future trouble... or perhaps unknowingly avoiding tremendous fortune. Who could say for certain?
Leon, without knowing any of those deeper implications, simply smirked coldly up at the overseer who was staring at him intently and with obvious hostile intent since he’d finished the second layer.
Then he chose decisively to make the trial private without hesitation.
[Private Trial Mode: ACTIVATED]
[All unauthorized observers being removed...]
In the very next moment, the overseer’s figure high in the air was suddenly enveloped completely by brilliant white light.
GLOW!
Velrith understood immediately what was happening the instant the light appeared around him. His fangs bared fully in pure rage.
The INSECT activated private mode! How?! That shouldn’t be available to someone at his level!
His resolve to finish this human completely became even more absolutely solid as diamond.
The very first second the protection period ends, I will personally start the systematic massacre of this entire world. Everyone dies.
He knew he would have to pay a substantial price for it—interfering directly in lower worlds carried serious penalties and costs that were not small even by his wealthy standards.
But for the secrets this human holds, and especially for the profound humiliation I’ve experienced from being called a worm... I will do this without hesitation in the future when the time arrives.
This debt will be paid in blood and screams.
The light intensified, and Velrith’s figure vanished completely from the arena space.
Leon, unaware of the specific murderous thoughts intensifying in the overseer’s mind, simply felt relief seeing the hostile presence disappear.
Finally. Now I can fight properly without holding back.
But alongside that relief, a distinct glint of cold resolve appeared in his eyes. His desire to grow stronger was reaching new heights—burning hotter than ever before.
He had a genuine sense of purpose and imminent crisis now, unlike anything he’d felt previously.
Even facing Archon Vyrra’s world and the upcoming looming threat there doesn’t give me this intense sense of crisis.
That situation had always carried the mental assurance of being able to escape into his own dimensional world if things became truly desperate.

However, he’d understood something critical recently: with his current mastery of space element principles, he now realized that escaping into his own world wasn’t nearly as safe as he’d assumed—especially against someone with high mastery of space element manipulation, or those with overwhelming absolute power and various specialized infiltration methods.
Running isn’t always an option. Especially against truly powerful beings.

However, Leon remained confident that Archon Vyrra, the red dragon guardian, and even the mysterious looming threat that had nearly engulfed Archon Vyrra’s entire world—including the figure who supposedly controlled armies of thousands—couldn’t achieve breaching his Dimensional Hourglass.
My dimensional treasure is not some random common artifact. It’s a genuine Mythical-ranked treasure.

Those beings simply wouldn’t have the specific capability to forcefully penetrate its defenses once he entered, especially now that the Dimensional Hourglass had evolved far beyond its original state.

Leon clearly remembered the previous system messages stating that it had surpassed standard Mythic rank classification and now possessed "potential beyond Divine Rank"—though he didn’t fully understand how impossibly high that actually ranked in the grand scheme of cosmic power hierarchies.
For now, I have absolute confidence in my ability to escape in moments of genuine crisis using the Hourglass.
But... I’m not sure at all that it would work against beings at that overseer’s level or higher. The gap might be too vast.
Shaking his head to clear away those spiraling thoughts, Leon forced himself to refocus on the present moment.
The most important thing right now is becoming stronger. With absolute strength, everything else will naturally fall into place.
Then Leon chose to continue the challenge without taking any rest at all.
The remnants of the previous match had already vanished completely, leaving the arena pristine once again.

He hadn’t used even one-thousandth of his total mana reserves in the previous encounter. With his Rank 7 affinity with ice element combined with extremely efficient energy usage, attacks of that level cost him almost nothing.
I could perform attacks like that essentially indefinitely without stopping, given my terrifying natural recovery speed.
In the next moment, a new message appeared—this time formatted differently:
[WARNING: Third Layer Difficulty Significantly Increased]
[Prepare Yourself]
[Trial Commencing in 5... 4... 3... 2... 1...]
It was the first time the tower had issued what seemed like a genuine warning, as if telling him to be seriously alert now.
Then—
FLASH! FLASH! FLASH! FLASH!
Hundreds upon hundreds of goblins materialized simultaneously across the arena in organized military formations.

But these weren’t the crude creatures from before. Each one wore complete bronze armor that covered their vital areas, and they wielded noticeably high-quality weapons—proper military-grade equipment rather than crude iron tools.
And at the very forefront of this small army stood a truly imposing figure.
A goblin wearing gleaming silver armor that seemed almost ceremonial in its quality. Its height was easily twice the size of the regular goblins—standing nearly as tall as Leon himself.
That’s...
